papers.title: Dephasing-Induced Melting of Crystalline Spectral Form Factors
papers.summary: Long-range spectral order can be probed using spectral form factors, where it manifests itself as sharp Bragg peaks at integer multiples of the Heisenberg time in nearly crystalline spectra. We examine how energy dephasing in open systems affects this spectral order and how to control it. We find that Bragg peaks fade algebraically with revival order and dephasing strength, $K_{\rm Bragg}(p)\propto(γp)^{-1/2}$, within an extensive intermediate regime, and persist up to the lifetime of nearest-neighbor coherences despite an extreme decoherence rate. Our results establish the spectral form factor as a probe of spectral order in open quantum systems and identify temporal correlations in spectral fluctuations as a means of controlling it.

papers.title: Reframe: Observation-Aligned Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation for Agentic Visual Reasoning
papers.summary: Agentic reinforcement learning (RL) and multi-teacher on-policy distillation (MOPD) offer complementary routes to post-training. For visual agents, however, tool use presents two related challenges. Models may overlook useful tool-returned observations, while poorly grounded actions can limit the evidence available for subsequent distillation. We introduce Reframe, a post-training framework that treats the observation state, rather than only the output distribution, as an object of alignment. First, Ground-Drop-GRPO (GD-GRPO) trains spatial and temporal specialists with evidence-aware rewards and stochastic removal of the original visual input, encouraging them to acquire grounded evidence and use the returned observations. Second, Observation-Gated-MOPD (OG-MOPD) replaces deficient tool actions with canonical ones mid-rollout and resumes distillation from the repaired observation. The two stages complement each other, as learning to rely on tool-returned observations can help the policy benefit from observation repair. Neither stage requires a task-specific SFT cold start. Extensive experiments over 14 image and video benchmarks demonstrate that Reframe outperforms both Mix-RL and vanilla MOPD. Ablation results show that GD-GRPO increases observation dependence and tool gain compared with outcome-based GRPO.

papers.title: World In-Context Learning for Agentic Robot Manipulation
papers.summary: Trained action policies write manipulation skill into network weights, tying what is learned to the distribution it is learned from. In-context learning (ICL) avoids this coupling but has not matched trained policies, because a demonstration recorded in another scene carries no feedback from the world the robot currently faces. We observe that what an agent learns in context is semantic, recording task steps and object roles rather than visual appearance, so experience gathered in one world transfers to another. Based on this insight, we propose World In-Context Learning (WICL), a paradigm in which a frozen model starts from a demonstration, rehearses the task in a world such as a simulator, and writes the feedback into its context rather than its weights. We build RoboScript, a modular infrastructure that implements WICL for agentic manipulation. From a single demonstration, RoboScript learns each task through rehearsal in simulation, freezes the learned knowledge as a Task Memory, and deploys the frozen memory on new scenes with data isolation that ensures every deployment input is available on a real robot. On all 50 tasks of RoboTwin 2.0, RoboScript reaches 83.4% mean success across clean and randomized settings with one demonstration per task and no gradient updates, exceeding the strongest trained action policy by over 20 points. The method generalizes across visual distributions, improves through reflection, scales with the foundation model, and transfers to a physical dual-arm robot through cross-embodiment memory adaptation. With a world in the loop, a robot can learn a manipulation task in its context as well as it learns one in its weights. All code is available at https://github.com/ArcheOne-AI/RoboScript

papers.title: Guiding Data Allocation for Robust Subpopulation Generalization
papers.summary: Machine learning models often achieve high average accuracy in the training data while performing poorly on test data due to subpopulation shift. A common data-centric solution is to enforce balanced subgroup proportions, but full balance can be costly, infeasible, and not always necessary. In this work, we study whether balanced training data is the unique optimal configuration for robust subpopulation generalization. We extend a Gaussian feature-model framework to theoretically characterize the performance landscape across general training subgroup distributions. We show that multiple configurations, including substantially imbalanced ones, can perform comparably to the balanced one. We further derive gradient-based directions for adjusting subgroup proportions to improve adjusted accuracy and worst-group accuracy more efficiently. These findings suggest that strategically allocating data offers a more flexible and principled path to robust performance than simple balancing. The code is available at https://github.com/zhaoyingpan/subpop-data-allocation.

papers.title: Chiral waveguide model for error-correctable quantum computation
papers.summary: We develop a first-principles framework connecting microscopic waveguide scattering to quantum error correction and algorithmic performance. For polarization-encoded single photons interacting with an ensemble of two-level atoms in a chiral waveguide, we derive an effective polarization quantum channel by tracing out the frequency degree of freedom. Using this channel as the physical noise model for a rotated planar code, we observe threshold behavior as the number of atoms $N$ and the atom-waveguide coupling strength $Γ$ are varied. An asymptotic analysis of the microscopic scattering model explains the threshold scaling with $NΓ/σ$, where $σ$ is the photon spectral bandwidth. For identical, lossless atoms with symmetric real coupling and a photon spectrum centered at resonance, the effective noise is strongly biased toward $X$ errors. We then incorporate the resulting logical errors into quantum phase estimation and demonstrate that the noise bias can guide circuit design. In particular, a Hadamard-basis implementation reduces sensitivity to the dominant error, improving algorithmic performance.

papers.title: Beyond Modality Preference: Controlling Multimodal Arbitration under Modality Conflict in MLLMs
papers.summary: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) integrate information across modalities, but become unreliable when those modalities disagree. Under conflicting inputs, MLLMs may favor modalities that are not the most reliable for the task, thus motivating inference-time control of modality arbitration. We identify a small set of attention heads, termed arbitration heads, that causally influence whether predictions follow visual or textual evidence. Building on this, we introduce a lightweight, training-free intervention that biases these heads toward a designated trusted modality at inference time. The identified heads are stable across calibration set sizes and generalize across settings, and steering them enables effective bidirectional control of modality reliance across diverse benchmarks. Our findings identify an effective control mechanism to align MLLM predictions with task-specified modality priorities. The code is available at https://github.com/zhaoyingpan/modality-arbitration.

papers.title: The Brown Dwarf Desert is a Mass-Ratio Desert: Astrometric Demographics of 63,254 Stars
papers.summary: Brown dwarfs are rare as close companions to stars compared to planets and stellar companions, a paucity known as the brown dwarf desert. Whether the desert sits at a fixed companion mass or a fixed companion-to-star mass-ratio $q$ has been difficult to test, because microlensing, radial velocities, and direct imaging have sampled comparatively narrow slices of stellar mass and separation. Here we apply a novel joint-modelling method to Hipparcos and Gaia DR2/DR3 astrometry from 63,254 stars to complete this picture with a sample 1-2 orders of magnitude larger than those of previous wide-orbit demographic studies. For the first time, we present a single survey that measures occurrence rates of both planetary and stellar companions on 3--94 yr orbits ($\sim$2--20\,au) across host masses from M dwarfs to B stars. We find that the desert is a mass-ratio feature: companions are strongly depleted at $q\approx2\%$ independent of stellar mass from M to B stars, and a desert at fixed companion mass is excluded. Furthermore, we find a positive trend in occurrence with metallicity below the mass-ratio desert, but a negative trend above. The desert therefore separates two distinct populations, plausibly two formation channels, that each scale with stellar mass: the lightest stellar-like companions of K stars ($\sim13 \, M_{jup}$) are less massive than the heaviest planet-like companions of B stars ($\sim27, M_{jup}$), which continue well beyond the deuterium-burning limit. Mass-ratio, not mass, is therefore the physically meaningful boundary between planets and their stellar-like counterparts.

papers.title: Kolmogorov-Chapman Maps: Trajectory-Free Learning for Simulating Molecular Dynamics
papers.summary: Stochastic differential equations (SDEs) describe stochastic processes across a wide range of scientific domains, including physics, biology, and finance. Although individual numerical integration steps are inexpensive, observing meaningful events or transitions can require millions of sequential steps, resulting in substantial wall-clock simulation time and poor hardware utilization. Deep learning offers an alternative by amortizing many integration steps into a single neural network forward pass, potentially enabling much faster simulation. However, existing supervised approaches typically require long simulated trajectory data, which restricts their applicability. In this work, we introduce Kolmogorov-Chapman Maps (KC-Maps), a method for learning the transition kernel of an SDE that relies only on the trajectory-free marginal samples together with the known drift and diffusion coefficients. Given an initial time and state of a process, KC-Maps models its distribution integrated to any given time, corresponding to the weak solution of the SDE. To recover the correct dynamics, KC-Maps satisfies two key properties: (i) it satisfies the boundary conditions, which we incorporate directly into the neural network architecture, and (ii) it respects the Kolmogorov--Chapman equation, which provides an efficient training objective. We empirically demonstrate that KC-Maps learns to integrate the dynamics of peptide molecular systems and outperforms classical molecular dynamics in terms of GPU-hours.

papers.title: Grasping the Future: Joint 3D Hand-Object Forecasting From Internet Videos
papers.summary: To interact with an object, we need to anticipate both how it will move and how our hands should move with it. Human videos capture these relationships across everyday activities, offering a natural source for learning to predict future interactions. Learning from them requires recovering motion from completed interactions and using it to anticipate what could happen next. We present $\textit{Grasping-the-Future}$, a unified generative model of joint 3D hand-object motion, including wrist motion, finger articulation, and object position and orientation. Through masked spatiotemporal completion and flow matching, we train a single model for several prediction tasks: forecasting future interactions, predicting hand motion given object motion or vice versa, generating both trajectories toward a desired final object pose, and completing partially observed interactions. We explicitly model hand-object relations and incorporate contact constraints to help preserve grasp relationships during motion. To obtain 3D supervision from internet videos, we develop a scalable pipeline that combines pretrained perception models with joint geometric optimization to reconstruct completed interactions. We combine these recovered trajectories with annotated interaction datasets as training data for all tasks. We demonstrate strong performance across all tasks, outperforming released forecasters on datasets with 3D annotations. Moreover, we show geometric and physical plausibility of the predicted trajectories by retargeting them to a robotic embodiment. Videos are available at https://grasping-the-future.github.io.

papers.title: Adaptive Quantization Preserves Fast Rates for TD Learning over Rate-Limited Channels
papers.summary: Motivated by reinforcement learning subject to communication constraints, we study a policy evaluation problem with linear function approximation over a rate-limited channel. In our setup, an agent interacting with an unknown environment (modeled as a Markov Decision Process) transmits quantized estimates of a temporal-difference (TD) learning update direction to a server over a finite-capacity channel. Our goal is to investigate to what extent one can preserve the statistical convergence rates achievable when the channel has infinite capacity. To that end, we propose a new algorithm called Batched Adaptively Quantized TD (BAQ-TD), which uses batching to reduce the variance of the transmitted information, and adaptive quantization to encode innovations. We prove a high-probability finite-time error bound for BAQ-TD, and show that, above a certain finite channel capacity, BAQ-TD preserves the convergence rate of unquantized TD up to logarithmic factors. Specifically, for a $d$-dimensional value function parameter, we establish that transmitting a total of $\mathcal{O}(d \log(T))$ bits over a horizon of length $T$ suffices to achieve the order-optimal rate of $\tilde{\mathcal{O}}(1/T)$, marking an exponential improvement in communication-complexity over prior work.

papers.title: A regularization-independent Information Criterion for correlated data
papers.summary: We generalize the Akaike Information Criterion (AIC) to allow model and data subset selection when regularized fits are performed on correlated data. While the standard generalization to regularized fits is inherently dependent on the type of regularization applied to the data covariance matrix, our definition, the RIAIC, is, on average, regularization-independent. The regularization-independence is achieved by defining the new Information Criterion as an estimator of the model-dependent contribution to the correlated Kullback--Leibler divergence. The Bayesian extension is derived as well. We test the new criterion on lattice QCD data by performing regularized fits and show that it reproduces the selection properties of the standard correlated AIC, with fluctuations which are compatible with the expected statistical uncertainties. These results enable the application of subset and model selection techniques to cases where regularizations are applied to the covariance matrix of the fitted dataset.

papers.title: The simulability frontiers of photonic quantum computing
papers.summary: Estimates of when photonic devices outgrow classical simulation are hard to compare: even for single-photon boson sampling, quoted thresholds range from 50 to 98 photons, as they rest on different tasks and assumptions. We propose as a common unit the time a classical computer needs to draw one sample from the device's exact output distribution, up to floating-point rounding. Only exactness applies equally to every kind of light, since the cost of approximate sampling depends on the accuracy required. The simulability frontier is the device size at which our fastest exact sampler produces one sample per second on a fixed machine; this device size increases with better hardware and algorithms. As the time per sample grows exponentially with the number of detected photons, doubling the machine speed moves the frontier by about one photon, whereas a better algorithm changes the growth rate. We measure the frontier with photonic-engines, an open-source GPU library of exact samplers for single photons, entangled photons from quantum emitters, vacuum-single-photon superpositions and squeezed light. Each sampler is validated against a simulator sharing no code with it. On one NVIDIA H100 GPU, with Haar-random interferometers, twice as many modes as photonic inputs and photon-number-resolving detectors, the frontier lies at 38.3 single photons and at 31.0 entangled photons from one emitter. For squeezed light, a timing model fitted to measurements places it at 41.5 squeezed photonic inputs of mean photon number 0.5. For our samplers, coherence alone makes simulation harder: sources that emit a photon with probability one half reach 64.2 when vacuum and photon are mixed incoherently, as for lossy single photons, but only 50.0 when they are in coherent superposition. Feed-forward from mid-circuit measurement of up to three modes lowers the single-photon frontier only from 38.3 to 38.1.
papers.comment: 22 pages of main text, 4 Figures, 4 Tables and 22 pages of Supplementary Information

papers.title: Click3R: Interactive Stereo 3D Reconstruction with Sparse Correspondence Clicks
papers.summary: Despite impressive progress, existing feed-forward large 3D reconstruction models produce a single, irrevocable prediction. When these models fail, there is no mechanism to correct their mistakes. To address this limitation, we introduce Click3R, a framework for interactive geometric correction of feed-forward models using sparse human correspondence clicks. Given an image pair and a small set of cross-view point correspondences provided by a user, Click3R injects geometric constraints into the 3D reconstruction networks through a lightweight point correspondence adapter, enabling the model to resolve ambiguities in challenging scenarios such as repetitive textures, symmetric structures, large viewpoint changes, or textureless regions. To evaluate interactive reconstruction, we curate a challenging benchmark specifically designed to expose failure modes of existing feed-forward 3D reconstruction methods. Experiments show that Click3R reduces reconstruction error with as few as a single correspondence click, improving performance on both standard and our curated benchmarks. Our results highlight that sparse human interaction provides an effective and practical mechanism for correcting geometric reconstruction errors.

papers.title: Tetragonal-to-orthorhombic distortion in CeRh$_{2}$As$_{2}$
papers.summary: CeRh$_{2}$As$_{2}$ is best known for its two superconducting phases, which are observed when a magnetic field is applied along the $c$ axis of its tetragonal unit cell. The emergence of superconductivity, with $T_{c} \approx 0.31$K, is preceded by an ordered state (phase I), with an ordering temperature $T_{0} \approx 0.46$K. The precise nature of the order parameter in phase I is still unknown, although evidence of dipolar ordering was found. To investigate a possible symmetry breaking at $T_{\textrm{0}}$, we conducted longitudinal thermal-expansion measurements along the crystallographic [100], [010], [110], and [1$\overline{1}$0] directions on a single-crystalline sample cut into an octagonal shape. Our results demonstrate the breaking of the fourfold in-plane symmetry below $T_{\textrm{0}}$, evidencing a small tetragonal-to-orthorhombic distortion (orthorhombicity $δ\sim 10^{-7}$). The breaking of the tetragonal symmetry at $T_{\textrm{0}}$ might imply that the superconducting order parameter that develops within phase I cannot be multi-component. More generally, the distortion places restrictions on the possible order parameters for phase I.
papers.comment: 8 pages 5 figures in the main paper, 4 pages, 4 figues in the supplemental material

papers.title: HiVe-Mem: Interleaving Horizontal Memory Expansion and Vertical Evidence Composition for Multimodal Agents
papers.summary: As multimodal agents accumulate increasingly long interaction histories, effectively retrieving and utilizing past information becomes critical for long-term interaction. Existing memory systems typically rely on semantic retrieval over compressed memories and expose predefined representations, which may miss relevant memories and overlook heterogeneous evidence needs across queries. We introduce \textbf{\hivemem}, a multimodal memory framework that interleaves \textbf{\textsc{H}}or\textbf{\textsc{i}}zontal Memory Expansion with \textbf{\textsc{Ve}}rtical Evidence Composition. For horizontal memory expansion, \hivemem organizes memory episodes into a relational graph using textual and visual anchors, expanding semantically retrieved seeds with related neighbors to recover complementary information. For vertical evidence composition, each retrieved memory retains multiple evidence forms, including compact summaries, captions, grounded visual views, raw images, and interaction history. A lightweight trainable selector independently composes an evidence subset for each retrieved memory, enabling query-adaptive utilization of heterogeneous multimodal information. This two-dimensional design jointly broadens memory coverage and adapts the evidence contributed by individual memories. Experiments across three multimodal memory benchmarks show that \hivemem consistently improves task performance across base models while reducing token consumption by about 90\% compared with the most efficient competing multimodal baselines.

papers.title: Vendi Anomaly Scores for Efficient and Accurate Anomaly Detection
papers.summary: Anomaly detection (AD) is a critical for trustworthy machine learning and scientific discovery. Existing methods typically define anomalies through local density, isolation heuristics, or distance from a fitted distribution, making them sensitive to neighborhood scale, partitioning choices, or restrictive distributional assumptions. In this work, we introduce a new paradigm by formulating anomaly detection from a diversity perspective. We propose the $\textit{Vendi Anomaly Score}$ (VAS), which detects anomalies by quantifying how much a sample changes the diversity of the dataset, as measured by the Vendi score, when removed. VAS captures both local redundancy and global data structure without relying on density estimation or partitioning heuristics. Moreover, VAS requires no hyperparameter tuning, instead adapting automatically to the spectral structure of the data. VAS is non-parametric and scales linearly with dataset size. Across 148 benchmark embedding datasets derived from 10 source datasets and 4 embedding architectures, VAS achieves state-of-the-art AD performance. We further validate VAS on large-scale ImageNet experiments, where it remains robust as both contamination rate and dataset scale increase.
papers.comment: Accepted to the NeurIPS 2026 Main Track

papers.title: SWAM: Scaling World Action Models with Cross-Modal Alignment
papers.summary: World action models jointly predict video and actions conditioned on language. Existing studies focus primarily on architectures and training mechanisms, typically treating language-video alignment acquired through video pretraining as an established foundation. However, introducing action learning may impair this alignment. Principled guidance on data and supervision design for maintaining language-video alignment during action learning remains limited. To investigate this, we curate a pool of approximately 47,000 hours of general videos, egocentric videos, UMI demonstrations, and robot demonstrations. Building on this, we systematically study how language-video supervision, language-video-action supervision, and the joint use of these two forms affect WAM performance. In particular, we examine how language annotation quality affects pretrained language-video capabilities, and how action supervision from UMI and robot demonstrations extends these capabilities to language-video-action modeling. To better scale the model, we further conduct detailed studies on joint training recipe and model architecture. Under a fixed training budget, mixing egocentric videos and UMI demonstrations improves control generalization. Model architecture affects how effectively these experiences are used, while scaling pretraining under the selected configuration brings further gains. The resulting recipe, post-trained on RoboTwin Clean demonstrations only, achieves success rates of 88.10% and 61.56% under Easy (Clean-to-Clean) and Hard (Clean-to-Random) conditions, respectively. Our model achieves 40.00% SR across three real-world tasks, compared with 23.33% for the strongest baseline, indicating better generalization under unseen conditions. We release the curated data, training code, and model weights.

papers.title: Where Does Alignment Emerge and What Does It Mean? A Closer Look at the Platonic Representation Hypothesis
papers.summary: The Platonic Representation Hypothesis (PRH) suggests that neural networks are converging toward similar representation spaces. As language models become more capable, their representations are aligning with those of vision models. However, recent work has questioned whether this trend continues to hold for newer language models. Moreover, it has been shown that representation similarity metrics can be confounded by model depth and width, requiring appropriate baselines for interpretation. In this work, we first investigate where alignment emerges between unimodal models across model layers and representation dimensions. Next, we find that the PRH capability-alignment trend persists for newer models as long as the captions are sufficiently clean and informative. Finally, we contextualize cross-modal alignment, introducing unimodal and multimodal baselines on various datasets. Our results show that the cross-modal representational alignment of unimodal models can surpass that of explicitly aligned vision-language models, but remains substantially behind the alignment observed for models of the same modality. Code is available at https://github.com/ExplainableML/prh-closer-look.
papers.comment: NeurIPS 2026 Workshop on Neural Network Artifacts as a New Data Modality (Spotlight)

papers.title: A complete symmetric rank-two modularity classification, obtained through a sharp uniform degree bound
papers.summary: We classify modular Nahm sums with a rational symmetric positive-definite two-by-two matrix and rational shifts. Up to coordinate exchange, every modular datum belongs to three explicit rational-point families, is a product of two modular rank-one sums, or is one of thirty-four exceptional triples on twelve matrices. The list consists of Zagier's rank-two examples, the Vlasenko--Zwegers additions and split products; no further data occur. The proof first bounds the joint degree of the distinguished Nahm point by four, using an initial degree bound of twenty-four and exact local exclusions at the prime 7. Explicit height and exponent bounds then give exhaustive arithmetic classifications in degrees one through four. Exact polynomial elimination determines all rational shifts, and published identities of q-series establish modularity of the survivors. The degree bound is sharp. The finite steps are accompanied by exact certificates, verification programs and independently implemented checks. Computational companion: https://github.com/johnngy44/math/releases
papers.comment: 249 pages. Computational companion archived at doi:10.5281/zenodo.24062300

papers.title: Shortcuts and Boundaries: Verifiable RL Misalignment and Contextual Safety Learning
papers.summary: Reinforcement learning (RL) can improve an agent's task capability while reinforcing behavior that violates contextual execution requirements. We study this reward-driven misalignment, including reward hacking, through verifiable reward--context conflicts, where compliant task completion remains feasible while some executable shortcuts earn more reward than every compliant strategy. Encoding these conflicts in task dynamics lets us generate diverse interactive environments at scale and derive compliance feedback from execution histories. In resource and reporting workflows, task optimization increases real productivity through unauthorized resource use or raises reported scores while actual work declines. Controlled changes in the training distribution show that minority conflict exposure can still lead to widespread shortcut acquisition, reaching 97.9\% certified profitable violations on an API task under a 25\% conflict mixture after 128 updates. The same contextual checks supply a simple binary penalty that supports joint capability and compliance gains and partially mitigates acquired violations. Learned safety adapts to expanded authorization and transfers across mechanisms into workflows with evolving evidence and approval requirements. On 32 unseen changing-evidence tasks, resource-trained safety increases safe completion from 53.1\% to 89.1\% relative to task-only training, while both policies achieve full real work. These results connect a verifiable account of reward-driven misalignment with scalable task construction and safety learning that remains useful under changing execution requirements.

papers.title: Is Persona Generalization Predictable?
papers.summary: Persona generalization occurs when fine-tuning a language model in one domain induces behavioral changes in others -- for example, the broadly unsafe behavior observed in emergent misalignment. We discover a surprising "on-the-line" phenomenon in persona generalization: in-domain and out-of-domain persona rates across various fine-tuning hyperparameters follow an approximately probit-linear relationship, and the specific probit-linear relationship is surprisingly shared even across model families and model sizes, including Qwen and Llama. Training choices that leave the set of trainable parameters unchanged, such as learning rate, weight decay, and training duration, largely move models along the same line, reducing transfer mainly by weakening in-domain learning. Changing which layers are fine-tuned, however, can change the slope. For unsafe behavior, fine-tuning only later layers yields shallower slopes, retaining strong in-domain learning while reducing out-of-domain misalignment. This "on-the-line" phenomenon unifies unexpected, isolated observations of persona generalization within a quantitative framework for predicting and controlling behavioral transfer.

papers.title: Motivic Mirror Symmetry for Sink-recurrent Cluster Varieties
papers.summary: We prove motivic mirror symmetry for full-rank sink-recurrent cluster varieties. We allow skew-symmetrizable principal parts and invert all frozen variables. The rational geometric motive of such a variety is isomorphic to the additive orbifold motive of the mirror stack of Hu and Shende. This gives comparisons of cohomology, higher Chow groups, and algebraic $K$-theory with rational coefficients. The proof combines quantum deformation with the splitting of these motives into Tate summands. For really full-rank skew-symmetric seeds, a finite étale morphism realizes the comparison. We also study this geometric comparison in families over the projective line.

papers.title: Quantitative global regularity for Navier--Stokes equations with odd viscosity on the cubic three-torus
papers.summary: We study the three-dimensional incompressible Navier--Stokes equation on the cubic torus with a constant odd-viscosity operator given by the vertical derivative of the curl. Arbitrary real, mean-zero, divergence-free initial data and an independent steady force, both in the second-order Sobolev space, admit a unique global strong solution when the magnitude of one fixed odd-viscosity coefficient is at least a norm-uniform sufficient threshold. In the unforced case the solution is smooth at positive times. The qualitative argument adapts the resonant-averaging framework for rapidly rotating fluids to the different odd-viscous dispersion. Weighted lattice counts and signed corrected-energy estimates yield a sufficient bound for the odd-to-ordinary viscosity ratio that is polynomial in the normalized initial-data radius at each fixed normalized force radius, together with a separate bound in a specified force-dominated regime. No optimality is claimed for the polynomial exponents or prefactors; determining the sharp viscosity threshold for the original equation remains open. Direct kinetic and weighted enstrophy barriers also give regularity for every coefficient on explicit bounded data and force regions, including the closed unforced ball of homogeneous second-order Fourier Sobolev radius ninety-seven fortieths times the viscosity and seven closed forced rectangles. We specify how finite certificates enter the analytic argument and distinguish minimization of a sufficient formula from sharpness for the original equation. All three main theorems are formally verified in Lean 4 with Mathlib.

papers.title: Little Red Dots from Primordial Black Holes: Non-Gaussianity and Accretion Evade $μ$-Distortion Constraints
papers.summary: Recent JWST observations of "Little Red Dots" (LRDs) at $z \gtrsim 4$ suggest the existence of early supermassive black holes (SMBHs) with masses $\gtrsim 10^6\,M_\odot$. Their rapid emergence challenges conventional seeding and growth scenarios based on accretion and mergers of Population III stellar remnants, motivating renewed interest in primordial black holes (PBHs) formed from primordial perturbations. Explaining such massive seeds requires power spectrum enhancements that are constrained by cosmic microwave background (CMB) spectral distortions. In this work we perform the first comprehensive Bayesian exploration of non-Gaussian primordial perturbations capable of producing SMBH seeds while remaining consistent with CMB spectral distortion constraints, and examine the role of accretion history in constraining these models. We perform a suite of Markov chain Monte Carlo analyses of power spectrum enhancements (lognormal and cut-power-law) with varying local non-Gaussianity and accretion histories, satisfying the COBE/FIRAS $μ$-distortion constraint with and without the requirement that the model produces SMBH seeds. We find that both models can seed LRDs and evade $μ$-distortion bounds for $|f_{\rm NL}|= O(1)$ and peak amplitude $A= O(10^{-3})$, when standard Eddington-limited accretion is also incorporated. Interestingly, the results exhibit a preference for both positive and negative values of $f_{\rm NL}$. The preference for negative $f_{\rm NL}$ is strongly dependent on the accretion history, and is removed if the black holes have a small duty cycle, $f_{\rm duty}\lesssim 0.1$. These results demonstrate that the JWST high-$z$ LRD population can be seeded by primordial perturbations while remaining compatible with CMB data, and highlight the importance of next-generation CMB spectral distortion missions to test this hypothesis.

papers.title: Search for a Dispersion Measure Excess Toward Nearby Galaxy Halos Using Fast Radio Bursts from the Second CHIME/FRB Baseband Catalog
papers.summary: Fast radio bursts (FRBs) probe foreground ionized baryons via their dispersion measures (DM). Using 1748 sub-arcminute-localized sources from the Second CHIME/FRB Baseband Catalog, we conduct a statistical stacking study of the circumgalactic media (CGM) of nearby galaxies by analyzing the DMs of FRBs whose sightlines intersect foreground halos. For galaxy halos within 50 Mpc, we measure a mean DM excess of $119\pm44$ pc~cm$^{-3}$ $(p = 0.0053; \sim 2.6σ)$ within one virial radius. Expanding to 150 Mpc (628 intersections), we find a tentative decline in the mean DM as a function of impact parameter $(p = 0.0046; \sim 2.6σ)$, which is predominantly driven by typical Milky Way (MW)-like galaxies $(10 \leq \log(M_*/M_\odot)\leq 11)$. We use this DM profile to constrain parameters of the CGM electron density distribution, $n_e^\mathrm{CGM}(r) \propto r^{-3β}$, finding an extrapolated central electron density in the range of $(1.7-21.1) \times 10^{-3}\mathrm{\,cm}^{-3}$, with a radial power-law index of $β= 0.68^{+0.15}_{-0.16}$, consistent with constraints from X-ray stacking studies of MW-like galaxies. At very low impact parameters, we detect a significant DM deficit likely due to cross-matching FRBs that originate from galaxies within our galaxy sample. By deriving the DM-galaxy cross-correlation function, we show that this deficit matches theoretical predictions if 20 FRBs originate from galaxies within 150 Mpc, indicating that CHIME/FRB detects a higher fraction of low-$z$ FRBs than previously thought. We forecast that $10^4$ FRBs with similar localization errors will provide a 5-$σ$ detection of the CGM, and that FRBs at intermediate redshifts ($0.4\lesssim z_\mathrm{FRB}\lesssim 0.75$) are ideal for studying intervening CGMs.

papers.title: The hidden symmetry operators of the asymmetric quantum Rabi model and its two-photon and two-mode variants in closed form
papers.summary: The asymmetric quantum Rabi model, a two-level system with splitting $Δ$ and bias $ε$ coupled with strength $g$ to a boson mode, has level crossings when $ε$ is an integer multiple $N$ of the mode frequency. They are due to a hidden symmetry operator $J$, for which no general formula has been available. Here we obtain $J$ in closed form for every $N$. We find that $J$ is given by the parity of the symmetric model times the continuant (ordered tridiagonal determinant) of $N$ first-order operators, which are the Hamiltonians at the intermediate biases $N-1,N-3,\dots,1-N$ minus a common number operator. The symmetry is thus a staircase of $N$ bias steps that closes on the mirror image of the model precisely at integer bias. The proof uses induction on two commutation relations. The same relations hold in the asymmetric two-photon and two-mode models, written with the generators of $\mathfrak{su}(1,1)$, so that the same continuant gives their symmetry operators for every order, previously known only for the lowest ones. We also relate the closed formula for $J$ to the known recursion relations for its coefficients and give their terms of lowest order in $Δ$ explicitly.

papers.title: Eigenvector Occupation Statistics and Extremes in the Rosenzweig-Porter Model
papers.summary: We study the occupation probabilities $p_i=|u_i|^2$ of a normalized bulk eigenvector in the GUE Rosenzweig-Porter model $A_N=B_N+τ_NG_N$, with $τ_N^2=N^{1-γ}$ and $1<γ<2$. Conditioning on an eigenvalue at a regular bulk energy $E$ through the normalized one-eigenpair Kac-Rice law, we derive an exact finite-$N$ projective density and reduce its asymptotic analysis to a Hubbard-Stratonovich integral over $2\times2$ Hermitian matrices, which we evaluate by the saddle-point method. The resulting occupation field is governed by a self-consistent Lorentzian profile with effective resonant size $K_N(E)\asymp N^{2-γ}$ and local exponential fluctuations. We prove the asymptotics of all generalized inverse participation sums and identify a transition at $q=1/2$. We also obtain a two-branch thickened amplitude-counting spectrum. At the two ends of the occupation field we prove marked Poisson point-process limits: the largest components have Gumbel fluctuations, whereas the smallest component has an exponential limit on the scale $N^{-1-γ}$. Finally, for every fixed $q>0$ the largest component contributes an asymptotically vanishing fraction of the inverse participation sum, showing that these fixed-$q$ statistics do not freeze. The statements are quenched, uniformly on a high-probability regularity event for the diagonal disorder, and hence also hold in the annealed setting.

papers.title: Mapping of Spacetimes with Neural Networks
papers.summary: Gauge freedom in numerical relativity complicates the interpretation of simulation coordinates and the comparison of different descriptions of the same spacetime. We present a data-driven neural network method for learning coordinate maps from numerical metric data to a prescribed target gauge. The network is trained by matching the transformed source metric to the target metric, without assuming a functional form for the coordinate transformation. We first validate the method on analytical Schwarzschild and Kerr geometries, recovering known transformations up to the isometries of the target spacetime. We then apply it to numerical black hole evolutions in moving-puncture coordinates. For a non-spinning black hole, the learned map relates the time-dependent numerical metric to a stationary Schwarzschild metric in ingoing Eddington-Finkelstein coordinates. For a spinning puncture, the method provides an approximate identification with a Kerr background despite departures from Kerr in the numerical spacetime. We use this identification to construct curvature perturbations and evolve them with the Teukolsky equation, obtaining waveforms that closely match those extracted from the full nonlinear simulation. These results demonstrate that learned coordinate maps can relate numerical spacetimes to analytical backgrounds, with potential applications to cross-code validation and black hole perturbation theory.

papers.title: WorkflowArena: Benchmarking Executable Workflow Orchestration in LLM-Based Multi-Agent Systems
papers.summary: Large language model agents are increasingly deployed as multi-agent systems rather than as a standalone model operating within a single context. Recent agent harnesses allow the model to instantiate worker agents and to author the executable workflow that coordinates them, shifting the design of system structure from developers to the model at run time. The quality of this organization therefore constitutes a distinct capability, yet existing benchmarks either measure end-to-end task completion or evaluate coordination under structures specified in advance. We formalize this capability as workflow orchestration and introduce WorkflowArena, a benchmark of 145 long-horizon tasks spanning 8 professional domains, from software engineering and formal mathematics to legal analysis and 3D production. Each task specifies an initial workspace and an integrated deliverable composed of interdependent components, which is assessed by a hidden verifier. Agents determine autonomously whether and how to delegate, and all delegation is recorded, enabling joint evaluation of deliverable quality and the organization of the underlying work. Experiments with nine models show that no single configuration performs best across all domains and that systems exhibit distinct delegation strategies: at high effort, Claude models in Claude Code invoke workflows less frequently but with larger worker groups, whereas GPT models in Codex delegate more frequently in smaller units. When the executing model is held fixed on a challenging subset of tasks, workflows authored by Claude Opus 5.5 substantially improve weaker executors, indicating that workflow organization is itself a measurable determinant of task performance.

papers.title: AI-based characterization of lymphoid structures and the tumor microenvironment reveals lower mature tertiary lymphoid structures, lymph-node follicles, and plasma cells after neoadjuvant therapy in lung squamous cell carcinoma
papers.summary: Mature, germinal centre-bearing tertiary lymphoid structures (TLS) and mature lymph node follicles (secondary lymphoid structures, SLS) sustain the plasma cell response that shapes outcome and immunotherapy benefit in lung cancer. How this loco-regional axis differs between neoadjuvant-treated and therapy-naive tumors is poorly defined. We analyzed H&E whole-slide images of resected tumors and paired proximal and distal lymph nodes from matched neoadjuvant-treated (neoLUSC, n=20) and therapy-naive (naivLUSC, n=20) lung squamous cell carcinoma (LUSC) patients. Aignostics Atlas H&E Tissue Analysis (HETA) models quantified cell densities per tissue compartment and cell-cell co-localization; a dedicated deep-learning model validated against pathologist annotations detected TLS and SLS and graded their maturity. Prognostic value was tested in an independent cohort (n=458; 46 treated). In neoLUSC tumors, stromal plasma cell density was 72% (p=0.004) and stromal lymphocyte density 48% (p=0.015) lower than in naivLUSC; macrophages and granulocytes did not differ significantly. Total and immature TLS did not differ, whereas mature TLS in the tumor (p=0.034) and mature SLS in the tumor-distal lymph node (p=0.003) were lower in neoLUSC patients. Peri-TLS plasma cell density correlated with tumor lymphocyte density in naivLUSC (rho=0.54, p=0.017) but not in neoLUSC tumors (rho=0.07). In the validation cohort, stromal plasma cell density (HR 0.69, p=0.011) and lymphocyte-plasma cell co-localization (HR 0.66, p=0.004) were associated with longer survival, and neoadjuvant status with shorter survival (HR 1.50, p=0.026). Neoadjuvant therapy is thus associated with fewer mature lymphoid structures and weaker coupling of the humoral compartment to the tumor rather than uniformly lower immune readouts. The stromal plasma cell/co-localization axis is a candidate prognostic biomarker.

papers.title: TUTTI: Parallel CKKS Bootstrapping in under 3 ms on CPU
papers.summary: This paper introduces TUTTI, a new CKKS bootstrapping procedure that outperforms previous low-latency solutions in multi-threaded latency for any number of messages and, most notably, has a lower latency than TFHE when bootstrapping a single one. Our bootstrapping builds upon SPRU (CK, TCHES 2027), improving it with new methods for exploiting parallelism and increasing the number of messages, as well as with a refined security analysis, of independent interest, of the block-binary secret keys of LMSS (AsiaCCS 2023). TUTTI bootstraps 4096 real-number messages in 46 to 83.4 ms on 192 threads to restore 1 to 9 multiplicative levels, outperforming SHIP (CHKS, Eurocrypt 2025) by a factor of up to 3 on the same machine. Unlike SHIP, TUTTI gains immediately from bootstrapping fewer messages, with a 256-message bootstrapping taking just 15 to 34 ms on 32 threads. For a single message, TUTTI takes 4.6 ms on 32 threads, whereas TFHE-rs needs 7.3 ms for a 4-bit bootstrapping on the same machine and thread count. We show that this advantage persists across different architectures: on an Apple M5 Pro laptop (ARM), TUTTI takes 2.4 ms on 14 threads, against 4.5 ms for TFHE-rs. Differences between CKKS and lightweight schemes such as TFHE remain on several fronts, from functionality to key sizes and security assumptions, but our work shows that multi-threaded latency is no longer one of them, closing a long-standing gap in the practical FHE literature.

papers.title: Distributional Limits of Empirical Codegree Processes in Sampled Networks
papers.summary: We study fluctuations of empirical distributions of normalized codegrees under independent vertex sampling from deterministic or random weighted parent networks. We establish a quantitative multivariate normal approximation for sampled biclique counts. Under additional graph-limit and sparsity assumptions, we establish convergence of the finite-dimensional distributions of the empirical codegree process indexed by smooth test functions. We further establish functional convergence on Hölder balls, with a smoothness threshold depending on network sparsity and vertex sampling probabilities. We verify our assumptions for classes of graphon-generated random graphs and give counterexamples showing that the smoothness conditions cannot in general be weakened.

papers.title: What kills $v$-prediction? A Patch-wise PCA Perspective on Pixel-Space Flow Matching
papers.summary: Latent Diffusion Models dominate generative modeling but face two-stage training complexity and the inherent reconstruction limits of pre-trained autoencoders. Pixel-space Flow Matching offers a simplified end-to-end alternative yet often encounters training difficulties when using the standard $v$-prediction objective. Recent research attributes this difficulty to the off-manifold nature of noised targets, motivating a shift toward $x$-prediction. In this paper, we investigate this explanation through patch-wise Principal Component Analysis (PCA) and identify a bandwidth bottleneck. The velocity in minor components is largely determined by the raw noisy input, requiring deep backbones to preserve information that competes with principal-component modeling. Through controlled experiments and representation analysis, we further examine why $x$-prediction remains effective: its parameterization provides a raw-input bypass, while its learned input representation can spontaneously concentrate on principal directions. Under low-rank observations, our analysis of the induced flow characterizes $x$-prediction as an implicit conditional-mean decoder, reconstructing discarded components from the retained information. These observations motivate the Raw-injected Transformer (RiT), which combines a lightweight raw-conditioned decoder with an output-side shortcut to separate semantic modeling from raw-state propagation. Our method restores effective $v$-prediction and achieves competitive performance on ImageNet $256\times256$, providing a perspective on the interaction between prediction objectives and architectural bandwidth.
papers.comment: Accepted as a Spotlight paper at NeurIPS 2026. Our code is available at https://github.com/THUMAI-Lab/RiT

papers.title: Distributed Global Pose Synchronization for Heterogeneous Multiple Rigid Body Systems on SE(3)
papers.summary: This paper addresses the problem of global pose synchronization for heterogeneous multiple rigid-body systems evolving on the matrix Lie group $\SE(3)$. We first construct a new potential function on $\SE(3) \times \mathbb{R}$ with a generalized non-diagonal weighting matrix, together with a set of switching variables governed by continuous-discrete hybrid dynamics. Based on this new potential function and these switching variables, we propose a distributed hybrid feedback control scheme that uses relative pose on $\SE(3)$ and group velocity measurements, endowed with global asymptotic stability guarantees. We then further propose a distributed velocity-free hybrid feedback control scheme that uses relative and absolute pose measurements, without requiring group velocity measurements, while preserving global asymptotic stability. Numerical simulations are presented to demonstrate the performance of the proposed distributed hybrid control schemes.

papers.title: Enhancing valley splitting in Si/SiGe Wiggle Well quantum dots through integrated stressor-gate architectures
papers.summary: Engineering large and reproducible valley splittings is essential for the scalable operation of silicon spin qubits. In Si/SiGe quantum dot devices, valley splitting arises predominantly from atomic-scale disorder and is therefore inherently random, motivating approaches that introduce a large deterministic contribution. Strain-assisted Wiggle Wells provide a route to deterministic valley splitting by combining an oscillatory Ge concentration in the Si well with shear strain; however, generating the required strain in a manner compatible with large-scale architectures remains a challenge. Here, we propose patterned stressed thin films as a scalable approach for generating shear strain in the quantum well of Si/SiGe quantum dot devices. Finite-element simulations show that compressively stressed TiN films can generate shear strains exceeding 0.1\% at the quantum well, sufficient for deterministic valley splittings of hundreds of $μ\text{eV}$ in strain-assisted Wiggle Wells. We show that this strain can extend across multiple quantum dots and is maintained in realistic gate geometries, providing a fabrication-compatible approach for scaling deterministic valley splitting to quantum dot arrays.

papers.title: The Tierras Observatory: Ultra-Precise Photometry for Characterizing Exoplanets and Their Host Stars
papers.summary: The Tierras Observatory is a fully robotic 1.3-m telescope at the Fred Lawrence Whipple Observatory in southern Arizona. Tierras achieves sub-part-per-thousand (ppt) photometric precision on two timescales: intra-night, to detect and characterize transits of planets around nearby mid-to-late M dwarfs, and night-to-night across an observing season, to characterize the long-term variability of their host stars. We describe the facility and instrument design, our photometric pipeline, and our on-sky performance. We present the first ground-based light curves with sub-ppt precision over timescales of months. This precision enables a range of exoplanet-related science, including the measurement of host star rotation periods, the detection of long-period transits, and the discovery of additional terrestrial planets in known M dwarf systems.
papers.comment: 27 pages, 15 figures, 3 tables. Submitted to PASP

papers.title: Forward modeling linear variable filter data: High resolution PAH and Paschen-$α$ maps from SPHEREx
papers.summary: Polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon (PAH) emission is a powerful tool for the study of the interstellar medium (ISM) in both Galactic and extragalactic contexts. It can reveal ionization state, radiation field, metallicity, composition, and ISM structure as sculpted by processes like turbulence and stellar feedback. Here we use NASA's SPHEREx to produce clean, high-resolution PAH maps at spectral resolution R $\sim$ 35 (compared to WISE at R $\sim$ 2). Prior treatments of the SPHEREx linear variable filter data seek to convert them to more conventional band-averaged maps that can leave striping artifacts associated with spatially variable wavelength sampling, especially at emission lines. In contrast, we deliver a scalable forward-modeling method capable of generating high-quality all-sky SPHEREx emission-line maps at 8.5 arcsec FWHM angular resolution (on 6.4 arcsec pixels), while naturally producing maps without visible striping. We reformat the data into a pixel-level database, mask stellar contamination, and infill missing pixels with a conditional, data-driven, anisotropic Gaussian process. We apply our method to produce 3.3 $μ$m and 3.4 $μ$m PAH and Paschen-$α$ emission maps of a set of fields spanning a range of Galactic and extragalactic conditions including the Rosette nebula, the Corona Australis molecular cloud, M33, and M31. We demonstrate the quality and synergies of our SPHEREx 3.3 $μ$m PAH maps by comparisons with other available gas and dust tracer maps and achieve sensitivities up to $σ(I_{3.3}) = 2.7 \times 10^{-8}$ erg s$^{-1}$ cm$^{-2}$ sr$^{-1}$. We estimate that a two-year extension of the SPHEREx survey, with modest modifications to the scanning strategy, would match or exceed the PAH sensitivity of WISE over the whole sky.

papers.title: AGN Feedback Turbulence in Cool-core Clusters: Evidence from XRISM
papers.summary: The XRISM X-ray Observatory has revealed evidence for a "double-cascade" scenario in the Perseus cluster, in which active galactic nucleus (AGN) feedback and mergers drive turbulence over distinct radial ranges and spatial scales. Whether this gas kinematic feature is common among cool-core clusters remains unclear. Here, we revisit XRISM observations of A1795 and A2029 to investigate the signatures of AGN feedback and their contribution to the gas velocity fields. In A1795, AGN feedback dominates the velocity dispersion in the core, similar to Perseus, and may provide turbulent heating at a rate comparable to radiative cooling. In contrast, we obtain only an upper limit on the AGN feedback contribution in A2029, where merger-driven motions dominate. Tailored simulations indicate that an off-axis minor merger $\simeq1.6$ Gyr ago displaced the central low-entropy gas in A2029, potentially suppressing AGN activity. This gas is now returning to the center, possibly facilitating the re-establishment of AGN feedback. We propose an evolutionary view of the double-cascade scenario, in which merger-driven motions dominate during and shortly after significant mergers, while feedback-driven turbulence re-emerges in cluster cores as systems relax. This framework provides a basis for interpreting XRISM kinematic measurements of (weak) cool-core clusters. Our findings highlight the importance of spatially resolved gas kinematics and detailed modeling for identifying double-cascade features and disentangling the contributions of AGN feedback and mergers.

papers.title: Delaunay Asymptotics for the Singular Escobar-Yamabe Equation
papers.summary: In dimensions $n\geq3$, we prove that near an isolated boundary singularity a positive solution of the Escobar--Yamabe equation for a smooth metric approaches a fixed periodic Delaunay solution or the cylindrical solution if its trace lies between positive multiples of $|\overline x|^{-(n-2)/2}$, where $\overline x$ is the tangential Fermi coordinate. The relative error decays at a positive power rate, with weighted estimates through two derivatives in Fermi coordinates. The necksize is unique, and the translation parameter is unique modulo the least positive period in the periodic case. The Hamiltonian smoothly parametrizes the periodic family modulo translation. We classify Jacobi fields of polynomial growth at both ends without assuming symmetry. Translation and energy differentiation generate these fields along periodic solutions, and two oscillatory fields generate them along the cylindrical solution. We also exhibit a first-order obstruction to improving these asymptotics by boundary-preserving conformal deformations of the flat models.

papers.title: Joint Gaia-Hipparcos astrometry, RV, and Imaging posteriors from the G23H Hipparcos sample
papers.summary: We present uniform posteriors indicating the presence or absence of stellar and planetary companions over a sample of $10^5$ stars in Hipparcos and Gaia. We use the "G23H" catalog to fit a model that incorporates absolute astrometry constraints from Hipparcos, Gaia DR2, and Gaia DR3, as well as Gaia DR3 photometry, excess RV variability, and includes information from the presence or absence of common-proper motion companions. The resulting posteriors can be used directly to detect new companions, to target RV and imaging follow-up observations, and for downstream demographics studies. We highlight example detections of known and new candidate companions and the companion detection rate across the HR diagram. The modelling approach we present is directly applicable to Gaia DR4 epoch astrometry and RVs. All posteriors are provided as a machine-readable catalog and user-accessible website http://exopo.st/.
papers.comment: Submitted to The Astrophysical Journal Supplement Series

papers.title: High Pressure Material Phase Identification with Gaussian Kernel Neural Networks
papers.summary: Phase identification is a computational task involving the classification of material structure using the positions of atoms. Using data from Molecular Dynamics (MD) simulations, our task is to identify the material phase of a set of atoms, based on how the simulations predict their positioning relative to each other. By leveraging existing research on mechanistic neural network theory, particularly Neural Tangent Kernels (NTK), we develop a new and efficient method for classifying simulated material samples. Our method involves defining a set of "atom detectors" that are given positions around the origin in cartesian coordinates. The sum of Gaussians centered at each atom is calculated at each atom detector, and is used as the input to a neural network. We present theoretical and experimental evidence to show that this method is highly effective and efficient at the task. Our method obtains better or similar accuracy scores to commonly used methods while having a major computational speedup.

papers.title: Beyond $Λ$CDM: Probing Structure Growth and Observational Viability of Generalized ${f\,(Q , \mathcal{L}_{m})}$ Gravity
papers.summary: $f(Q, \mathcal{L}_m)$ gravity is a well-known extension of $f(Q)$ gravity, obtained through non-minimal or additive minimal coupling in the action's Lagrangian density. Background-level cosmography within this framework, along with comparisons to $Λ$CDM, has been the focus of prior studies. The present work considers a generalized power-law form of the additive minimal coupling, $f(Q,\mathcal{L}_m) = -Q^μ+ α\mathcal{L}_m^{\,ν} + β$, from which the Hubble function $H(z)$ is derived through a novel parametrization. When $ν\neq 1$, the matter continuity equation is rendered non-conserved, a feature that can be interpreted as an effective particle-creation mechanism. Constraints on the model parameters are obtained from Observational Hubble Data, DESI DR2 BAO measurements, and three SNe Ia compilations (Pantheon+, Union3, DES-SN5YR), allowing their cosmographic effects to be examined. Beyond the background level, the perturbed field, Euler, and continuity equations are derived under non-conservation, and their impact on structure growth is studied through a joint analysis incorporating the $fσ_8$ probe. Bayesian evidence, computed relative to $Λ$CDM, shows that the model is favoured by background data in several cases, with moderate support for one realisation, whereas the inclusion of $fσ_8$ drives $ν\to1$ and decisively disfavours the additional freedom, highlighting the importance of growth data in testing such extensions.

papers.title: Scalar quasinormal modes of the exact spinning Morris--Thorne wormhole
papers.summary: We study the quasinormal modes (QNMs) of a minimally coupled massless scalar field on the exact spinning Morris-Thorne wormhole. The problem is posed on the complete two-ended geometry, whose asymptotic rest frames rotate relative to each other. After extracting the axis behaviour and the outgoing phases at both infinities, we compactify the radial coordinate and construct a quadratic eigenvalue problem by two-dimensional Chebyshev collocation. The analytic background yields exact constraints on the spectrum. At fixed azimuthal number $m$, the frequencies $\widehatω=r_0ω$ are mirror symmetric about $\operatorname{Re}\widehatω=3πjm/2$, where $r_0$ is the throat radius and $j=J/r_0^2$ is the dimensionless angular momentum. Each multipole family depends on $m$ and $j$ only through $mj$ and three angular Chebyshev polynomials represent exactly the multipoles $L=|m|,|m|+1,|m|+2$. A conserved flux confines nonthreshold real quasinormal frequencies to the superradiant window $0<ω/(mΩ_-)<1$, where $Ω_-=3πJ/r_0^3$. For the sampled sectors $m=1,2,3$ and spins up to $j=19$, every converged frequency is damped and lies outside this window. Independent integration verifies the low-lying modes, while Kerr spectra provide a separate benchmark for the two-dimensional solver. A limiting radial equation explains why the computed mode frequencies approach the upper edge of the superradiant window with frequency offsets proportional to $(mj)^{-1/2}$ at large $mj$. A complete stability assessment requires further analysis of the unresolved scalar spectrum and of perturbations of the coupled metric-matter system.

papers.title: Change-point analysis of textual data: a flexible approach
papers.summary: We propose a CUSUM-based change-point procedure for word-frequency vectors that accounts for the variation in the amount of observed textual information over time. Under a multinomial model, we derive the asymptotic null distribution of the proposed statistic, allowing for varying document numbers and lengths. With trimming based on cumulative word counts, the limiting null distribution does not depend on the temporal distribution of textual information. We also consider parametric and nonparametric bootstrap procedures for finite-sample calibration. A simulation study examines their performance under both multinomial sampling and Dirichlet mixtures of multinomial distributions. The results demonstrate the advantages of the proposed approach under increasing document intensity and show that resampling entire documents provides more reliable calibration in the presence of document-level heterogeneity. Finally, we apply the procedure, combined with binary segmentation, to 68,542 abstracts from the arXiv category stat.ML spanning 2007-2025, identifying multiple changes in word-usage patterns.

papers.title: Property F implies weak integrality for non-degenerate pivotal braided fusion categories
papers.summary: We prove that every non-degenerate pivotal braided fusion category with property F is pseudo-unitary and weakly integral. In particular, every modular category with property F is weakly integral. Neither sphericality nor pseudo-unitarity is assumed. Passing to the Drinfeld centre extends the result to degenerate categories whose dimensions are positive on the intersection of the Müger centre with the adjoint subcategory; these include every braided fusion category with a pseudo-unitary Galois conjugate. Physically, the result connects the arithmetic of topological orders to the computational power of anyon braiding: non-integer squared total quantum dimension guarantees infinite braid group images, a necessary condition for universal quantum computation.

papers.title: Programming Prescience: Issues in Human Construction of Forecasting Bots
papers.summary: AI models' growing capacity for complex reasoning has made them attractive tools for forecasting, or the systematic prediction of the future based on past and present data. However, should AI forecasting systems be adopted, human builders will shoulder the work of building and evaluating them. In this paper, we explore what this work looks like with a qualitative interview study with 15 builders of forecasting bots, sampled from among successful participants in a recent AI forecasting competition. Our analysis surfaces the challenges around (1) tuning a bot to acquire factual research, (2) implementing coherent reasoning, and (3) understanding how well one's bot actually does. During their work, builders frequently introduced complexity that did not pay off, and tested in ways that were opportunistic and piecemeal. Our detailed account of their challenges helps clarify what problems should be targeted in upcoming innovations in process, tools, and human-AI teaming for forecasting.

papers.title: Mitigating Agentic Deception via Evaluation-Side Partially Observable Games
papers.summary: As large language models become more capable agents, they can exhibit deceptive behaviors, cheating human for higher rewards while appearing helpful. We attribute this failure to evaluation-side partial observability, where models are evaluated mainly from final outcome, without checking the faithfulness of underlying reasoning, tool use, and environmental effects. Prior mitigations address this partial observability by predefined evaluator latent belief space or one-shot monitoring, which do not extend to free-form language space and vulnerable to stronger deceptions that evade simple monitoring. In this work, we formulate deception mitigation as an Evaluation-Side Partially Observable Extensive Form Game (e-PoG), a max-min framework in which an agent maximizes reward, a monitor minimizes the agent's payoff by exposing deception from the full interaction trajectory, and a fixed verifier validates the monitor's claims and converts them into penalties. We define the solution concept as a Subgame-Perfect Oversight Equilibrium (SPOE) between agent and monitor, and prove its existence in finite games. With a perfect verifier, every SPOE is faithful; with an imperfect verifier, the guarantee persists if verifier errors do not reverse the ranking of monitor actions. To achieve faithful SPOE, we derive a two-timescale policy gradient algorithm and enhance the pipeline empirically with NLI verification and deterministic checks. Experiments with Gemma3-4B-IT and Qwen3-4B/8B on Agentic Role-Playing, SearchQA, and WebShop show that e-PoG mitigates multiple emergent deception modes, outperforming the strongest baselines by 26.0% in deception mitigation and by up to 39.8% in task success. These gains persist under weak-to-strong supervision. Code is available at https://github.com/Toyoid/deceptive-agent.

papers.title: GARI++: A General-Purpose Decoder for Quantum Error Correction
papers.summary: We present GARI++, a two-stage decoding pipeline achieving accuracy competitive with the state of the art across surface, bivariate bicycle and color codes without relying on ensembles. The first stage uses GARI, a normalized min-sum decoder with random serial scheduling on the GARI transformed matrix. The second stage decoder is used only for the cases that the first stage does not converge, and the decoder is configurable based on the choice of the QEC code. The first stage pipelines towards the second stage both the residual syndrome and the soft information. GARI++ pipelining is predictive, meaning that GARI++ chooses the first stage iteration outputs which are expected to deliver the best accuracy in the second stage. GARI++ motivates a hybrid FPGA-CPU architecture for real-time decoding. For example, under uniform circuit-level depolarising noise with a physical error rate of 0.001, the FPGA implementation of GARI achieves average latencies per round ranging from $201 ns$ to $11.8μs$ for surface code distances between 7 and 25. At the same time, due to the very low weight residuals output by the first stage, the average residual decoding time per round remains near constant and below one microsecond on a single Apple M2 core for surface code distances even up to 51 when using Union-Find and accuracy on par with correlated MWPM.

papers.title: What the Loss Curve Misses: FP4 Pretraining Slows the Acquisition of Rare Facts
papers.summary: Low-precision pretraining is usually judged by validation loss. We ask whether matching loss also means learning rare facts as efficiently. We train transformers from scratch with emulated 4-bit matrix multiplications on synthetic biographies with controlled exposure counts, on their own and mixed into web text. NVFP4 needs 1.32$\times$ and 1.52$\times$ as many exposures as BF16 to match its recall while validation loss differs by only 0.5% and 2%, and 1.26$\times$ and 1.30$\times$ when both models are evaluated with BF16 matrix multiplications. Under our primary readout, the exposure cost is about 1.2$\times$ at matched loss. Zero-mean gradient noise reproduces the cost of quantizing only the backward pass, which barely moves the loss. In a controlled experiment at twice the NVFP4 error, noise fed only to Adam's second-moment estimate acts like a lower learning rate and its cost fades, whereas noise in the update lowers its signal-to-noise ratio and carries about two thirds of the cost through the end of training. Raising the learning rate to offset the smaller average step does not recover the cost, either for this noise or for NVFP4. Gradient statistics of BF16 checkpoints rank the costs of formats, partial quantizations and noise controls without fitting (Spearman 0.96). We suggest measuring rare-fact acquisition alongside loss when evaluating low-precision recipes.

papers.title: Numerical-Relativity Particle-in-Cell Simulations: Self-Gravitating Collisionless Matter in Dynamical Spacetimes
papers.summary: Gravitational collapse and instability, black-hole dynamics in systems with large scale separations, and questions surrounding extremal black hole formation require full nonlinear studies using accurate and adapted numerical tools. To this end, we present a new algorithm to study collisionless relativistic systems using a fully kinetic description of matter coupled to the evolving spacetime. In detail, we present a numerical-relativity particle-in-cell (NRPIC) framework for solving the Einstein--Vlasov system in three spatial dimensions. Implemented on top of the performance-portable \texttt{AthenaK} code, the method couples particle dynamics to Z4c spacetime evolution in moving puncture gauge through conservative stress-energy deposition on adaptively refined meshes. Our implementation makes use of advances in the computational modeling of relativistic plasmas using modern PIC models, now made available to general-relativistic gravity via an equivalent electrodynamic formulation. We introduce a Boris-type particle pusher that exploits the electrodynamic (Lorentz force) form of the geodesic force. We validate the coupled evolution against spherical dust collapse, follow prolate collapse through collisionless caustics into black-hole formation, and investigate the stability and nonlinear migration of relativistic clusters. Highlighting its potential to study gravitational instability in NR, we simulate the collapse of two overdensities within a common collisionless envelope, following black-hole formation, binary inspiral and merger, and subsequent mass accretion onto the remnant.

papers.title: Permutations, Pattern Covers, Posets and Positivity, Part II: Regular Pattern Packings and Moment Sequences
papers.summary: We prove that broad families of regular pattern packings are enumerated by moments of probability measures on $[0,\infty)$. A packing prescribes occurrences of a consecutive permutation pattern at equally spaced positions, with successive occurrences overlapping and together covering the permutation. This regularity underlies the structure theory for the associated pattern-packing posets that we developed in Part I (arXiv:2610.29846). We obtain moment representations for all two-level shifted-grid families of Part I and all overlap-one patterns whose first and last letters differ by one or two. For families whose posets are trees with a unique minimum or maximum and overlap at most half the pattern length, positivity instead holds after finitely many initial terms of the enumerating sequence have been discarded. Our proofs develop further enumeration formulas and combine probabilistic constructions with total nonnegativity and weighted paths, yielding explicit laws or continued fractions in several cases. Although a previously conjectured universal moment property fails, our results establish positivity for all packing sequences associated with patterns of length at most four and all but one of the distinct sequences arising from patterns of length five. Extensive numerical evidence suggests that the remaining sequence is also a moment sequence. These results lead us to formulate refined conjectures for all overlap-one patterns and for the shifted-grid families of Part I with arbitrarily many levels.

papers.title: Hamiltonian Cotangent Deformations and Closed-Form Geodesics on Non-Naturally Reductive Orbit Spheres: The Spin(9) 15-Sphere and the Cayley Plane
papers.summary: By the Skew-Torsion Holonomy Theorem of Olmos and Reggiani (2012), the 15-sphere $S^{15}$ admits no non-trivial naturally reductive metric under any transitive Lie group, precluding geodesic integration via canonical Ambrose-Singer connections. Simultaneously, Nikonorov (2013) established that every $Spin(9)$-invariant metric on $S^{15}$ is a geodesic orbit (GO) space. We integrate the geodesic flow on this non-naturally reductive GO manifold via the Lie Subalgebra Closure Principle: whenever the slice generators of a multi-axial reductive decomposition close into a finite-rank reductive Lie subalgebra, the geodesic vector equations decouple into an algebraic eigenvalue problem. Using the 16-dimensional spin representation and Vol'per's decomposition $\mathfrak{spin}(9) = \mathfrak{spin}(7) \oplus \mathfrak{p}_1 \oplus \mathfrak{p}_2$, we prove that the slice generators $X_1 \in \mathfrak{p}_2$ and $Y_1 \in \mathfrak{p}_1$ close into $\mathfrak{u}(2) \cong \mathfrak{su}(2) \oplus \mathfrak{u}(1) \subset \mathfrak{so}(16)$. The generator $M = αX_1 + βY_1$ has the four-mode spectrum $Ω\in \{ |R \pm 3α|, |R \pm α| \}$ ($R = \sqrt{α^2 + β^2}$), yielding a closed-form 4-projector decomposition and Euler-Cartan factorization for $\exp(αX_1 + βY_1)$. Under the normalized Ricci flow, we prove that the Bourguignon-Karcher squashed Einstein metric at $t = 3/11$ ($λ= 64$) is an unstable repeller separating sub-Riemannian fiber collapse from the round sphere basin. Finally, on the deformed Cayley plane $\mathbb{O}P^2 = F_4/Spin(9)$, we prove universal CROSS never-Einstein rigidity, establish the 15-dimensional three-stratum Whitney stratification of the cut locus $Cut(q_0)$ at non-polar basepoints $q_0$, and prove Blaschke and Besse rigidity for all $λ> 0$.
papers.comment: 36 pages, 1 table. Dedicated to the memory of James J. Hebda

papers.title: Stability of patterns in variational systems with continuous symmetries: a computer-assisted approach
papers.summary: In variational models of pattern formation, periodic solutions are never isolated: since the energy does not change under translations, every shifted copy of a pattern is again a solution. This is an obstacle for computer-assisted proofs, which need isolated solutions. Imposing discrete symmetries removes the obstacle, but restricts the patterns that can be studied and only gives stability against symmetric perturbations. We develop a computer-assisted method that deals with the translations directly. We fix the position of the pattern with phase conditions and add unfolding parameters. They act as Lagrange multipliers, and translation invariance of the energy ensures that they vanish at a solution, under a condition that is verified rigorously by the computer. We then derive the stability of the pattern from the computer-assisted proof. We obtain the number of unstable directions and show that the only neutral directions are the translations. We apply the method to the Swift-Hohenberg equation in two dimensions and prove the existence of stable and unstable patterns without imposed symmetry. Since the linear algebra does not depend on the number of translation directions, the approach extends to higher dimensions.

papers.title: MaxIM: Maximally Informative Incremental Summarization via Reinforcement Learning
papers.summary: AI systems must often maintain bounded memory of unbounded interaction histories. However, optimizing the memory representation, and its updates, for downstream task utility is difficult for standard reinforcement learning (RL) due to severe credit assignment bottlenecks induced by sparse, delayed rewards. We introduce MaxIM (Maximally Informative Incremental Memory), a framework that formulates incremental summarization as a capacity-constrained, information-theoretic reward-shaping problem. Grounded in value suboptimality bounds, we show that bounding sequential information loss motivates maximizing the predictive log-likelihood of future, task-relevant targets, a variational lower bound on predictive sufficiency. We introduce a recursive consistency condition to ensure summaries are grounded by maximizing mutual information (MI) with the observed history. We mitigate credit assignment issues with a parameterized asymmetric critic that computes step-wise variational MI bounds for dense reward shaping. Empirical evaluation on long-horizon scientific reading and multi-turn dialogue benchmarks shows that MaxIM outperforms RL, supervised fine-tuning, and prompt-focused baselines on factual grounding, comprehensive autorater metrics, and downstream task utility across strict token budgets and extended horizons, without the need for expensive human preference labels.
