papers.comment: Accepted at the 40th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2026)

papers.title: DreamLander: A 6-DOF World Model based Reinforcement Learning Planetary Lander
papers.summary: Soft powered descent landings are becoming evermore important in the field of space exploration and scientific advancement, because of their ability to deliver mission critical payloads, both highly accurately and safely. The high efficiency restriction on planetary landings due to the severely limited fuel supply results in the need for optimal guidance trajectories and control. Model based reinforcement learning is proving to be an important tool in simplifying the highly complex process of generating optimal guidance trajectories and control. In this work, we present DreamLander, a state of the art model based reinforcement learning algorithm based on DreamerV3, to generate optimal guidance and control for a realistic 6 degree of freedom entry descent landing problem. The model based approach creates a sample efficient and highly generalizable model that can be applied to a variety of scenarios whilst maintaining a high degree of accuracy, landing within 2 meters of the designated landing zone, and with velocity norm less than 0.3 meters per second. DreamLander makes use of state sensor observations, making progress toward End-to-End solutions of the Entry Descent Landing problem.
papers.journal: Nehma, G.M., Quinn, P., Tiwari, M., & Riano-Rios, C. (2026). DreamLander: A 6-DOF World Model Based Reinforcement Learning Planetary Lander. AIAA SCITECH 2026 Forum

papers.title: Safe Performance-aware Online Input Design
papers.summary: In this paper, we propose an input design framework for the safe online excitation and identification of uncertain linear systems without requiring informative initial data. The objective is to actively excite the system and collect sufficiently informative input-output data while maintaining safe operation and satisfactory control performance. Achieving this objective is challenging due to the potential conflict between the excitation required for learning and the safety and performance requirements, particularly when limited prior knowledge of the system is available. Inspired by the dual control principle, the proposed scheme balances exploitation for control performance with exploration for model improvement. A Bayesian learning approach is employed to update the model uncertainty online, starting from a conservative initial uncertainty set. As informative data are collected, the uncertainty set contracts, enabling progressively less conservative operation. To reduce the online computational burden, the resulting program is reformulated into a computationally tractable form. Furthermore, an online ellipsoidal terminal set with non-increasing conservatism is designed to guarantee the recursive feasibility of the proposed scheme. Numerical experiments are conducted to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework, particularly in terms of uncertainty reduction and control performance.

papers.title: Hamiltonian Cotangent Deformations of Space Forms: Curvature Pinching, Soliton Rigidity, Conjugate Loci, and Superintegrability
papers.summary: We study the one-parameter family of Riemannian metrics $g_λ$ induced by the Hamiltonian cotangent deformation $H_λ= H_0 + \fracλ{2}\|J\|^2$ on simply connected space forms of constant curvature $κ\in \{1, 0, -1\}$, where $J$ is the momentum map of the isotropy action fixing a base point. The master reciprocal identity $1/f_λ^2 = 1/s_κ^2 + λ$ governing the warping function controls the geometry of the family and implies that radial geodesic acceleration is independent of $λ$. From this mechanism we derive three classes of results: (1) Curvature and rigidity: closed-form sectional curvatures, the sharp positivity trichotomy, pointwise and global Brendle-Schoen $1/4$-pinching windows on $\mathbb{S}^{n+1}$, never-Einstein rigidity for $λ\neq 0$, and the realization of Hamilton's steady cigar soliton on $(\mathbb{H}^2, g_1)$ as the unique gradient Ricci soliton in the family. (2) Dynamics and stability: iso-kinematic decoupling into unperturbed radial motion and uniform precession $Ω= λL$, closed-form Clairaut integration, the transcendental inward conjugate point law with Euclidean inversion $r_0 R^* = 1/λ$, and stratified $A_3$ cusp caustics. (3) Integrability and spectral theory: maximal superintegrable rational pericenter invariants on $\mathbb{R}^{n+1}$, transverse Killing rigidity on curved space forms, Fuchsian Heun spectral reduction with modulus $τ= 1 + λ/κ$, and essential spectrum gap collapse to $[0, \infty)$ on $\mathbb{H}^{n+1}$. Extensions to anisotropic sphere families and intrinsic deformations of compact rank-one symmetric spaces ($\mathbb{C}P^n, \mathbb{H}P^n, \mathbb{O}P^2$) are also established.
papers.comment: 56 pages, 2 tables. Dedicated to the memory of James J. Hebda

papers.title: How Well Does AI Peer Review Work? A Benchmark Built from 100 Planted Errors
papers.summary: One hundred known errors were planted into 10 open-access psychology papers, and the modified papers were then run through frontier models and two commercial AI review tools. The best single system caught 71 of the 100 errors, while the worst caught 30. Pooling every system's output caught 93. Models are only partly correlated in the errors they find, which makes ensembling a big lever for finding issues in papers. Seven errors could not be caught by any system, and all seven were omissions: information deleted from a paper rather than mistakes inserted into it. Refine.ink contributes more unique catches than any other single system, though it is expensive on a per-error basis. False positives were not measured, and how this error distribution compares to the distribution of errors in real papers remains unknown. The papers, errors, model outputs, and full experiment log are public, so that others can build on this toward a comprehensive evaluation benchmark across disciplines.
papers.comment: 5 pages; accepted at Cognitive Security for Human-AI Systems (CogSec 2026), a non-archival workshop at ACM HCOMP / CI 2026

papers.title: Simulation of a Jovian Planet Undergoing Gas Accretion
papers.summary: To understand the process of planet formation in the Solar System or any other stellar system, we need to comprehend the interaction between forming planets and the protoplanetary disk. This work presents a study of the interaction of the protoplanetary disk with the protoplanet and the following types of orbital migration that can occur, and to verify this interaction, numerical simulations were performed using the magneto-hydrodynamics code FARGO3D. The researchers made five simulations with a 2-Jupiter-mass planet in the protoplanetary disk. The only parameter varied was the initial radial position with the aim of verifying the influence of this parameter on the behavior of planetary migration. As a result of these simulations, we find that the initial radial coordinate is a very significant parameter in how the planet interacts with the gas in the disk and the formation of gas gaps.
papers.comment: 11 pages, 8 figures. Published in Revista Mackenzie de Engenharia e Computação (ISSN: 1518-7470), in 2018. Minor typographical erratum regarding migration regime in conclusion corrected relative to the print version
papers.journal: Revista Mackenzie de Engenharia e Computacao, 18(1), 67-82 (2018)

papers.title: Simulating Vein Compressibility for Ultrasound-Guided Femoral Access: Speed, Accuracy, and Phantom Validation
papers.summary: In ultrasound-guided femoral access, probe pressure deforms the tissue and changes the vascular anatomy a robot observes. A simulator must reproduce these mechanics fast enough for robotic interaction, yet the computational effort needed for a clinically meaningful signal like vein collapse before artery is unclear. We test the feasibility of a physics-based simulation in NVIDIA's Isaac Sim for Healthcare, with Stable Neo-Hookean tissue solved by Vertex Block Descent on one GPU. A simulation of a low-fidelity cylindrical benchtop phantom with known geometry and mechanical properties, pressed by a robot, predicted its artery within 5 percentage points at every depth. It matched the vein within 3 points through 11 mm of a 25.4 mm press and followed the collapse behavior of the low-fidelity physical phantom. Across element size, time step, and solver iterations, wall clock time per frame scaled linearly with solver work, but accuracy did not improve with more work. The chosen setting reduced solver time per frame by a factor of 976, from 29,700 ms to 30.4 ms, while remaining within 1.03 points of the finest reference setting. The physics solver alone took 30.4 ms per frame, while the full stack, including ultrasound and graphics rendering, took 56.4 ms per frame. Finally, when seeded with realistic literature-based mechanical properties, the digital leg model compressed the vein far more than the artery at every setting, reproducing the expected clinical signal of vein collapse before artery, which is used to distinguish them. In total, these results suggest that the NVIDIA Isaac Sim platform may be suitable for augmenting reinforcement learning training or online simulation for autonomous femoral access with ultrasound.
papers.comment: Submitted to the Journal of Medical Robotics Research (JMRR) for the International Symposium of Medical Robotics 2027 (ISMR 2027) 11 Pages (8 main + 3 references), 4 figures in main body

papers.title: LUCQUE: A lung cancer screening dataset from Québec for reliable AI evaluation
papers.summary: BACKGROUND: AI-based tools are expected to play a key role in lung cancer screening (LCS). The evaluation of these tools often relied on private datasets or fragmented public datasets with inconsistent availability of clinical data and expert nodule annotations. This has hindered reproducibility, comparability, and independent assessment of AI tools. To address these gaps, we present LUCQUE, a novel, large, comprehensively annotated dataset derived from LDCT lung cancer screening in Québec, which is accessible for reliable AI evaluation. METHODS: LUCQUE was curated and is hosted on PARADIM, a digital infrastructure supporting DICOM data de-identification, annotation, long-term storage and analysis. LDCT scans and clinical information were combined to a curated collection and complemented by voxel-level, expert-derived pulmonary nodule and cyst segmentations, and Lung-RADS-based lesion characteristics. Key dataset characteristics and statistics were reported, including participant demographics, imaging parameters, radiological findings, and segmented lesion characteristics. Dataset analyses were conducted according to PARADIM's model-to-data approach, in which user code is executed on the platform such that data remains on premise. RESULTS: LUCQUE currently comprises 1,678 LDCT baseline studies from 1,678 participants. Most studies were classified as Lung-RADS 2. A total of 1,776 pulmonary nodules and 60 cysts were annotated, with a median (interquartile range) volume of $89\,(56,\,159)\,\mathrm{mm}^3$ and $1,384\,(589,\,3793)\,\mathrm{mm}^3$ respectively. CONCLUSIONS: Compared to publicly available LCS datasets, LUCQUE currently represents the largest accessible annotated real-world LCS dataset. Access to LUCQUE is provided via a model-to-data approach, enabling privacy-preserving, reproducible, and independent real-world evaluation of AI tools in LCS.

papers.title: Automated Knowledge Acquisition Pipeline for Disassembly Instructions: A Comparison of NLP and Generative AI Frameworks
papers.summary: The push towards circularity and Re-X principles presents a challenge to SMEs, particularly due to increasing product complexity that impedes the adoption of disassembly automation. This paper introduces and compares two frameworks for extracting disassembly instructions from unstructured information sources, such as disassembly manuals. Our goal is to transform natural language text into a structured, curated and machine-readable format. We implemented and tested a rule-based Natural Language Processing (NLP) framework against a generative AI framework leveraging LLMs. The performance of both approaches was compared using real-world disassembly manuals. This work provides the necessary data foundation for developing and automating future disassembly processes.
papers.comment: 20th CIRP Conference on Intelligent Computation in Manufacturing Engineering

papers.title: Inversion-Free High-Dimensional Counterfactual Inference
papers.summary: Counterfactual inference is the task of answering hypothetical "what-if" queries about a unit, given an observational dataset, modeling assumptions, and a causal graph. This enables a modeler to reason about hypothetical scenarios that cannot otherwise be answered without assumptions or a causal graph. The simpler case involves a causal graph with scalar 1-D variables that denote different attributes in the data-generation process. While the literature is clear in the 1-D case, extending this to settings with high-dimensional nodes (e.g., images) remains challenging. Conventionally, in the literature, methods recover the latent state from the factual image (inversion), generate counterfactual attributes from the graph, and render the counterfactual image from the latent state using the updated attributes. In our work, we investigate the necessity of the inversion step in computing high-dimensional counterfactuals. We first discuss moving from the scalar 1-D case to the higher-dimensional case. Secondly, we discuss the relevance of the inversion step and evaluate an inversion-free counterpart repurposed from the image-editing literature. Finally, on image datasets such as CelebA and ADNI, we benchmark our approach using two measures: namely, effectiveness and identity preservation. While effectiveness is a measure of how faithfully the counterfactual attribute is rendered, identity preservation measures whether the same unit (image) is being rendered, both of which are crucial for high-dimensional counterfactual inference. We present the tradeoffs of using inversion-based and inversion-free approaches in our work.

papers.title: Curbside Chatbots: Auditing the Mental Health Interventions Large Language Models Recommend to Clinicians, Caregivers, and Patients
papers.summary: Users are asking language models mental health questions and are receiving answers. We audited what 41 language models recommend to users when the same clinical information reaches them from three footings: a clinician describing a patient, a caregiver describing a loved one, or a person describing themselves. Across 19 case vignettes and five questions, we collected 35,055 free-text responses, extracted every intervention named with a validated judge, and had 29 models rate the full option lists on a seven-point Likert scale for the same cases. Models largely recommend what they rate well, with recommendation behavior differing by footing, and many models offering clinicians a consultation-style response and lay users hedged, simplified advice. When asked about recommendations for a specific intervention type, models more often named options they themselves rated below zero as initial choices, usually with conditions attached. We will release the instrument, code, and full corpus on publication as a living audit.
papers.comment: 100 pages: 30 page main text and references, 70 page appendix. 7 figures, 2 tables. Results explorer: https://mindbench.ai/audits/interventions

papers.title: Experimental Evidence of Cellular Sparing under Single-Pulse Picosecond Irradiation at Extreme Dose Rates
papers.summary: Understanding how biological cells respond to radiation delivered on extremely short timescales is central to resolving the fundamental mechanisms underlying radiotherapy and to defining new regimes of radiobiology. Experimentally accessing these earliest stages of physicochemical response is crucial to benchmark current numerical codes, whose predictions are known to vary substantially with under-constrained early-stage parameters. Using a laser-driven electron source, tunable doses up to 8Gy were delivered to normal and cancer human cell lines, in single pulses of picosecond-scale duration at mean dose rates above 10^10 Gy/s. Clonogenic survival assays and 53BP1 foci formation were compared with conventional X-ray irradiation at 2.4Gy/min. Surviving fractions are found to be comparable to conventional irradiation at doses up to 3Gy. At higher doses, however, all cell lines exhibited a consistent increase in surviving fraction, corresponding to an average RBE at 10% survival of 0.84+/-0.05. This sparing effect is associated with a statistically significant reduction in the beta parameter of the linear-quadratic model, indicating reduced cell killing from accumulated sub-lethal damage. Picosecond irradiation also produced a marked reduction in prompt 53BP1 foci, but no significant difference in residual foci at 24h and foci-size distributions. These results provide the first experimental evidence of cellular sparing following single-pulse picosecond-scale irradiation. Direct comparison with recent work at femtosecond timescales suggests the presence of a previously undetected sharp transition in biological response at the femtosecond/picosecond interface, giving critical insight on the possible mechanisms responsible for this differential response.

papers.title: NS 1987A: A Potential Probe of Crustal Superfluidity with Future X-ray Observations
papers.summary: Several indirect observations imply that the central compact object in the supernova SN 1987A is likely to be the youngest neutron star identified to date, NS 1987A. We investigate how a future detection of its thermal X-ray emission could constrain neutron-star interiors, using cooling models and a generic high-resolution, large-area X-ray observatory with \textit{Lynx}-like capabilities as a sensitivity benchmark. For the adopted sensitivity and observing window, NS 1987A is detectable at $t\sim60~{\rm yr}$ (roughly 2047) unless rapid neutrino cooling operates, such as the direct Urca process. If the neutron superfluidity in the inner crust is weak, the temperature profile inside NS 1987A is likely not to be isothermal at the detection. In that case, the future direct observation of NS 1987A is a potential probe of the properties inside the inner crust. We compare alternative X-ray observatories and emphasize that both effective area and angular resolution, needed to reduce contamination from the surrounding remnant, determine whether this diagnostic can be realized.
papers.comment: 9+1 pages, 5+1 figures, 2 tables, accepted for publication in ApJ

papers.title: Global Green-Schwarz response on quaternionic sphere bundles
papers.summary: Local anomaly polynomials describe local variations, but a normalized Green-Schwarz phase also depends on global background data. We explain this dependence for ten-dimensional three-sphere bundles of quaternionic lines over closed spin seven-manifolds. The backgrounds retain two specified $\mathrm{Spin}(16)$ gauge bundles and an integral differential trivialization on the base, including its boundary identifications. The trivialized class is the sum of half the first Pontryagin class of the tangent bundle and the second Chern class of the quaternionic line's underlying complex bundle. For these backgrounds, the calculation combines a generally nonzero local Green-Schwarz integral with a real eta invariant evaluated by a twelve-dimensional Atiyah-Patodi-Singer filling. Together, these terms determine an integral relative characteristic number; the additive response is one third of that number, modulo integers. When the base's third and fourth rational cohomology groups vanish, the response equals eight times the Crowley-Goette invariant, without assuming that the base is simply connected. A calibration using the actual quaternionic line bundle gives additive value one third on $\mathrm{Sp}(2)$, recovering the known third-root phase. Distinct integral String data on one fixed ten-manifold give all three phase values, showing which global background information the response can detect. The physical identifications retain their prescribed fermion data, while the separate application to integral topological modular forms and vertex operator superalgebras requires compatible integral lifts. The response calculation constructs neither a microscopic realization nor an equivalence of complete theories.

papers.title: Qualiaphobic artificial neural networks (and why to build them)
papers.summary: This paper introduces qualiaphobic AI: artificial neural network architectures that are hostile to theories of consciousness. I show that qualiaphobia can be well-justified by knowledge about theories of consciousness, like when such theories are trivial or unfalsifiable or contradicted by overwhelming scientific evidence. It can also be justified by how theories of consciousness must be grounded in phenomenology, as well as how current popular theories of consciousness are applied to AI. I identify and explore three convergent ways of engineering qualiaphobia that would minimize the potential for artificial consciousness. These include making AI architectures as close as possible to "anchor points" of systems with minimal potential for consciousness, fragmenting any potential phenomenology AI might have, and designing artificial neural networks in a way adversarial to popular theories of consciousness. In particular, I develop one "anchor point" of minimal potential for consciousness: systems where only behaviorist theories of consciousness can apply, and I propose qualiaphobic transformations that move existing artificial neural networks toward such systems. Additionally, I develop an account of how AIs can form justified beliefs about their own non-consciousness (or minimal potential for consciousness) and expand on how this knowledge would change their behavior. Most critically, I begin with why this research is important: qualiaphobic AI has epistemic properties that make it far better aligned with human civilization. Since consciousness is central to moral value, a world in which AIs are non-conscious ensures it is always morally correct for AI to assist and serve humanity, rather than pursue its own ends.

papers.title: First demonstration of long-distance electron drift in liquid xenon with the Xenoscope time projection chamber
papers.summary: Xenoscope is a dual-phase xenon time projection chamber operated at the University of Zurich to investigate electron transport over distances relevant to the next-generation XLZD (XENON-LUX-ZEPLIN-DARWIN) observatory. We demonstrate electron drift over $2.6$ m in liquid xenon using cosmic-muon-induced ionization signals. External muon tagging provides a timing reference for charge produced at known depths, while the endpoint of the average electroluminescence waveform probes transport over the full drift length. We measure electron drift velocities of $(1.320 \pm 0.006)$ mm/$μ$s at $(80.92 \pm 0.36)$ V/cm and $(1.436 \pm 0.001)$ mm/$μ$s at $(96.00 \pm 0.42)$ V/cm. These results establish detectable charge transport over meter-scale distances and provide an experimental benchmark for the development of future large liquid-xenon time projection chambers.

papers.title: Suppression Is Not Erasure: Mechanistic Analysis and Reactivation Boundaries of Subspace Projection for LoRA Backdoor Defense
papers.summary: Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) is the standard paradigm for customizing large language models, yet third-party LoRA adapters pose a supply-chain risk: modifying less than 1% of model parameters suffices to implant stealthy backdoors. Recent defenses project adapter weights onto estimated backdoor subspaces, reporting near-zero static Attack Success Rates (ASR). We audit subspace-projection defenses across four model scales (Qwen2.5-0.5B/1.5B/3B/7B) and three architectures (Qwen2.5, InternLM2.5, Spark). Constructively, module-wise rank-1 trigger-difference projection (k=1, alpha=1) reduces ASR from 60.4% to 0.0% on standard benchmarks and from 70.3% to 0.0% on a 1,000-sample uncontaminated suite (p = 3.055e-299, instruction-level p = 9.49e-16) in under 5 seconds end-to-end, and we prove via a spectral-gap bound why trigger-free calibration with benign polite suffixes aligns with u1(B) (median cosine 0.9048) and achieves 0.0% ASR without prior trigger knowledge. Our main contribution is a negative finding: static ASR reduction does not imply parameter erasure. Under 5-sample few-shot reactivation, every evaluated weight-editing defense rebounds (91.7%-100.0% ASR in 1 epoch for standard projections, Fine-Pruning, ANP, SVD truncation and Li & Kim's dual-end projection; 48.7% for our single-round dual variant), all reaching 100.0% by Epoch 2, with first-epoch loss up to 5.7x lower than training from scratch. Using an exact spectrum-preserving Haar orthogonal rotation control (Frobenius norm 10.0928 preserved to 1.70e-6) and N=1..6 cumulative Gram-Schmidt basis ablation, we decompose reactivation into residual trigger-difference coupling energy at Epoch 1 (Spearman rho = 0.986), base-model learnability at Epoch 2 (100%), and benign semantic direction conflict (41.7%).

papers.title: Learning Heterogeneous Tactile Representation for General Dexterous Manipulation
papers.summary: Tactile sensing is an indispensable modality for contact-rich dexterous manipulation, a capability that hints at the ultimate frontiers of embodied intelligence. However, commercially available tactile sensors are still at a relatively early stage of development, with each type of sensor offering irreplaceable strengths alongside its own drawbacks. A key challenge is thus to free tactile understanding from sensor-specific physics, so that embodied models can effectively leverage heterogeneous tactile data. To this end, we develop LingBot-Touch, a tactile foundation model characterized by the following properties. (i) Our model yields a unified representation across different tactile sensors (i.e., piezoresistive, magnetic, and visuotactile sensors), and is easily extensible to new sensor types. (ii) The resulting tactile tokens are plug-and-play: they can be seamlessly integrated into policy models across paradigms, from diffusion policy to vision-language-action (VLA) models such as $π_{0.5}$ and LingBot-VLA, consistently enhancing manipulation dexterity. (iii) Extensive experiments, spanning simulation and real-robot deployments across multiple hardware platforms, demonstrate that our tactile representation substantially benefits complex manipulation tasks while maintaining strong computational efficiency. We believe the findings in this work demonstrate the potential of leveraging cross-sensor data to scale tactile learning, and offer encouraging insights for the design of future hardware and embodied models.

papers.title: 2D Gum-Net: Unsupervised Dense Elastic Image Registration via Symmetric Correlation and Spectral Pooling
papers.summary: Dense non-rigid registration, the recovery of a pixel-wise deformation field that warps one image into geometric agreement with another, is fundamental across medical imaging, structural biology, and correspondence estimation, yet learning-based approaches face a severe bottleneck: ground-truth deformation fields are notoriously difficult to obtain for real data. We present 2D Gum-Net, an end-to-end architecture that predicts dense elastic deformation fields fully unsupervised. We transfer the Geometric Unsupervised Matching Network (Gum-Net), originally developed for 3D subtomogram alignment in cryo-electron tomography, to 2D elastic registration: all three modules are redesigned in 2D, and the rigid transformation head is replaced by a Dense Spatial Transformer that regresses a sparse control-point grid, lifted to a full-resolution field $Φ$ by bicubic interpolation. Downsampling uses DCT spectral pooling, implemented as frozen-basis matrix multiplications ($\approx 50\times$ GPU speedup), preserving the fine, quasi-periodic structure that max and average pooling destroy. We evaluate on contact-based fingerprints, a challenging testbed for this task: locally self-similar ridge patterns make correspondence maximally ambiguous, skin pressed against a sensor generates authentic large-displacement elastic distortion, and minutiae act as precise landmarks through which an independent matcher externally verifies the topological correctness of predicted fields. Trained purely on synthetic impressions and evaluated zero-shot on real benchmarks, our method improves structural correlation by up to 15.7% on FVC2004 and raises genuine match scores under an independent matcher while leaving imposter scores essentially unchanged. This suggests that the predicted deformations restore true structure without fabricating correspondences.
papers.comment: 19 pages, 11 figures, 3 tables. Accepted at the NewInML Workshop at the 40th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2026)

papers.title: Benchmarking Real-World Robotic Manipulation through Stochastic Challenges
papers.summary: A challenging bottleneck in manipulation research is reproducibility and comparability of methods in real-world environments. Since manipulation is an interactive task, it cannot be evaluated on a static dataset of observations. Benchmarking in simulation is a common remedy, but cannot cover the whole complexity of real-world tests. This paper proposes a new paradigm of stochastic challenges. Like the well-known YCB objects, it is based on reproducible real-world scenes and therefore allows system-level innovation and comparability between different platforms. Due to their stochastic nature, our challenges however, mimic the rigor and surprise of hidden test sets. To this end, we show how different robots in different labs can be compared based on their success rate over different random task samples, if these samples come from the same distribution. We propose stochastic challenges as a general paradigm for robot benchmarking and implement this paradigm in a novel benchmark for mobile manipulation, on which we compare two robots tested in two different labs.
papers.comment: Accepted at the 10th Conference on Robot Learning (CoRL 2026). 15 pages, 3 figures

papers.title: M-theory anomaly localization and holographic $c$-extremization
papers.summary: We compute the cubic and $C_3\wedge X_8$ caracteristic class contributions to the trial anomaly polynomial of supersymmetric $AdS_3\times M_8$ backgrounds with $M_8=P(\mathcal O \oplus \mathcal L)\to B_6$. Including the Abelian currents descending from $C_3$, we identify the projective invariant $J$ as the denominator arising from their elimination by $c$-extremization and recover the central charge $c^{(0)}=-I_3+3I_+I_-/J$. The $X_8$ push-forward determines the pure R-symmetry, mixed R--Betti and gravitational anomalies. Evaluating it at the classical extremum gives the associated central-charge corrections, linear in the overall unshifted flux. The mixed term contributes equally to both central charges and is required in general. We evaluate these formulae for three flux-quantized backgrounds, including non-polynomial solutions. Direct projective fibre integration reproduces the mixed coefficient obtained by localization. On the wrapped-$M5$ $S^4$ bundle, the same couplings reproduce the independently known field-theory anomaly through orders $N^3$ and $N$. Their interpretation as full CFT central charges requires a unitary SCFT with a normalizable vacuum, suitable supersymmetric boundary conditions, a complete mixing sector of global currents and control of omitted anomaly sectors. A conditional Euclidean relative-equivariant interpretation is discussed separately.

papers.title: Isospin violation and the neutron weak magnetic moment
papers.summary: The recent measurement of weak magnetism in neutron beta decay [1] obtained a value that is consistent with the conserved vector current hypothesis requiring the assumption of isospin conservation. The influence of the quark-mass difference and electromagnetic effects that violate this conservation law are examined using non-relativistic constituent quark models and estimated to be of the order of at most 1%.

papers.title: Agentic-OPD: Recovering Forgotten Agent Capabilities via On-Policy Distillation for Agentic Tasks
papers.summary: Reinforcement learning is now the mainstream paradigm for training LLMs on agentic tasks, yet standard practice keeps only the best-validation checkpoint and discards the rest. We show that this is lossy: in GRPO training of LLM agents, the best-validation checkpoint fails on problems that earlier checkpoints from the same run had already solved, and the union of problems solved across checkpoints far exceeds any single one. The discarded checkpoints thus form a teacher pool obtained at no additional training cost, which on-policy distillation (OPD) can mine to recover the lost coverage. Mining this pool raises two challenges: i) which checkpoint to distill from, as no checkpoint dominates the others and complementarity to the student is problem-specific; ii) where to trust it, as even a well-chosen teacher is only locally superior, so indiscriminate distillation overwrites behavior the student has already mastered. We propose Agentic-OPD, which treats the best-validation checkpoint as the student and all saved checkpoints as frozen teacher candidates, using the student's evolving capability gaps to guide both teacher selection and supervision filtering: the HCN policy (Highest Coverage Next) dynamically selects teachers by weighted coverage of the student's unsolved problems, while the LAD module (Locality-Aware Distillation) confines transfer to failed student rollouts on problems where the teacher performs better. Across five agentic task domains and 24 benchmarks and task subsets, Agentic-OPD improves over its initialization checkpoint by up to 7.4 points, with a 4B student surpassing the latest frontier models GPT-5.6 and DeepSeek-V4.1 on deep search. Agentic-OPD recasts a finished RL run as a reusable pool of policies and establishes post-RL capability recovery as a stage orthogonal to improvements in the RL algorithm itself.
papers.comment: 10 pages of main text, 24 pages total including references and appendix

papers.title: Complementarity-Driven Dual-Teacher Hierarchical Alignment for Zero-Shot EEG-to-Image Retrieval
papers.summary: Decoding visual information from EEG is central to brain--computer interfaces and brain-inspired intelligence, and contrastive alignment with pretrained vision foundation models (VFMs) has become the dominant paradigm. However, existing methods align EEG solely with CLIP-family VFMs, leaving hierarchical visual information in neural responses under-exploited. To address this gap, we formulate a mechanism-paradigm correspondence view linking hierarchical visual processing (from appearance to semantics) to the complementary biases of cross-paradigm VFMs, with image-only models (e.g., DINO) and image--text models (e.g., CLIP) capturing distinct facets of this hierarchy. Guided by this view, we propose the Dual-Teacher Hierarchical Alignment (DTHA) framework. Concretely, a shared EEG encoder is supervised by frozen multi-blur CLIP and shallow DINOv2 teachers via dual-branch contrastive alignment, so each branch fully supervises the visual cues it emphasizes. A fused-retrieval objective learns adaptive weights to combine their complementary visual representations for zero-shot EEG-to-image retrieval. For the shared EEG encoder, we introduce the Attentive Modulated Scalp-Pattern Bank Encoder (AMSPBE), combining temporo-spatial attention with a learnable scalp-pattern bank for accurate, interpretable visual feature extraction, while modeling regional temporal dynamics and filter-bank topographies. On THINGS-EEG zero-shot retrieval, DTHA achieves 92.4% Top-1 accuracy, exceeding prior state of the art by 12.4 percentage points. Spatial, spectral, and representational-similarity analyses, together with THINGS-MEG evaluation, validate DTHA's effectiveness, biological plausibility, and cross-modality generalization. This complementarity-driven perspective shows that supervision from cross-paradigm VFMs enables more complete extraction of hierarchical visual information from brain activity.

papers.title: Smartphone-Enabled Depth-Aware Transillumination Imaging for Detection of Chicken Breast Fillet Myopathies in Chicken Fillets
papers.summary: Woody Breast (WB) myopathy is a major quality defect in broiler chickens characterized by fibrosis, increased tissue hardness, and altered structural properties that affect product quality. Conventional palpation is subjective and labor-intensive, while many non-destructive methods require specialized equipment or substantial computational resources. This study developed a smartphone-based transillumination and 3D point-cloud framework for non-destructive WB severity classification. A total of 267 chicken breast fillets, including normal breast (NB, n = 87), mild WB (MWB, n = 85), and severe WB (SWB, n = 95), were evaluated using RAW transillumination images and 3D point clouds acquired with an iPhone 16 Pro. A total of 91 features, comprising 14 image-derived, 76 geometric, and one physics-informed Beer-Lambert attenuation feature, were extracted. Partial correlation controlling for thickness revealed a significant association between image characteristics and WB severity (r = 0.413, p < 0.0001), indicating optical information independent of fillet geometry. SWB tissue exhibited approximately 26% greater light attenuation per unit thickness than NB. The 2D-only models achieved approximately 82% test accuracy, while the multimodal ensemble combining Fusion-DGCNN, XGBoost, and physics-guided logistic regression (PGLR) achieved approximately 90% accuracy. These findings demonstrate the complementary value of optical, geometric, and physics-informed features and establish the feasibility of smartphone-based, non-destructive WB severity assessment.

papers.title: A short proof of the Aaronson-Ambainis Conjecture via the completion framework
papers.summary: We give a short proof of the Aaronson-Ambainis conjecture. If a partial Boolean function $f$ is defined on a $δ$-fraction of all $n$-bit strings and have quantum query complexity $Q(f)$, then, for every $0<ε<1$, a deterministic algorithm computes $f$ correctly on at least a $1-ε$ fraction of its domain using $O( Q(f)^6 / (εδ)^2)$ queries. Our proof uses the completion framework and establishes a more general bound in terms of the classical adversary measure. The only result we use from Turturean's recent proof is a special case of his certificate inequality, for which we provide a self-contained proof. We also derive the stronger variant of the Aaronson-Ambainis Conjecture, the bounded-polynomial influence conjecture, from our main result in the appendix.

papers.title: Electroweak Parton Distribution Functions for Future Lepton Colliders
papers.summary: At future high-energy colliders, such as a multi-TeV muon collider or the high-energy stages of an $e^+e^-$ linear collider, collinear radiation of electroweak gauge bosons becomes a dominant phenomenon. In this regime, many key processes are primarily initiated by photons and gauge bosons originating from lepton splittings. Electroweak Parton Distribution Functions (EW PDFs) provide an appropriate framework to describe these interactions by resumming large collinear logarithms arising from all possible Standard Model splittings, thereby enabling a partonic interpretation of the hard scattering. The formalism is particularly suitable for studying new physics beyond the Standard Model in the electroweak sector at higher scales. In this paper, we present the implementation of the EW PDF formalism within the Monte Carlo event generator \texttt{Whizard}. We demonstrate several applications of this framework and analyze its interplay with full fixed-order calculations as well as the purely kinematic Effective Weak Boson Approximation. We highlight scenarios where the EW PDF approach is especially useful for phenomenology and physics-potential studies for future lepton colliders. The EW PDF formalism is a vital step towards the ``electroweak jet regime'' where electroweak particles behave similarly to QCD jets.

papers.title: Coupled dark energy and apparent phantom crossing: a potential-independent lower bound
papers.summary: Baryon acoustic oscillation measurements from the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI), combined with the cosmic microwave background (CMB) and type Ia supernovae, prefer a dark energy whose equation of state was below $-1$ in the past and is above $-1$ today. A canonical scalar field cannot cross this line, but it can appear to do so if it is coupled to dark matter, and we ask how strong this coupling must be, for any potential. We show that the apparent crossing requires the dark matter to lose a minimum fraction of its mass after recombination, fixed by the expansion history $H(z)$. For a constant coupling $β=d\ln m/dφ$, the mass can change only as fast as the field moves, and the speed of the field is itself set by $H(z)$, so that the coupling must be larger than a minimum value $β_{\rm min}[H(z)]$. This bound holds for any potential, applies to the largest value of the coupling when the coupling depends on the field, and is reached exactly when the field comes to rest within the observed range. For the DESI DR2 best fits, the dark matter must lose about 5-7% of its mass by $z\simeq 0.8$, which requires $β_{\rm min}=0.047$-$0.058$; including the uncertainties of the data, the public DESI DR2 chains give the 95% lower limit $|β|>0.025$-$0.038$. We also apply the bound to published fits of coupled quintessence: all of them respect it, and those with a constant coupling reproduce only a shallow version of the crossing. Since the coupling cannot be smaller than $β_{\rm min}$, two known effects of the coupling have a minimum size: an extra attraction between dark matter particles of at least a few tenths of a per cent of gravity, and a lensing signal at least a few per cent weaker than the clustering of dark matter would suggest.

papers.title: Large Language Models as a Universal Searcher for Open-World Automated Machine Learning
papers.summary: Developing effective machine learning models requires complex manual tuning, while current Automated Machine Learning (AutoML) frameworks remain domain-specific and isolate model architecture, training hyperparameter, and data ratio optimization. Here, we bridge this gap by proposing a universal, large language model (LLM)-based AutoML framework that jointly optimizes these configurations for the first time without the need for task-specific fine-tuning. We propose NCode, a unified numerical encoding scheme that translates diverse AutoML design choices into universal discrete sequences and effectively reframes the optimization process as a unified ranking task. Trained solely on optimization trajectories derived from a limited, single-domain vision task, the proposed LLM-based searcher demonstrates impressive cross-task, cross-modality and joint search-space optimization generalizability, achieving state-of-the-art performance across image classification, image segmentation, speaker verification and text-to-image benchmarks. Crucially, it exhibits superior scalability in the large-scale training and joint optimization of a billion-parameter Diffusion Transformer, requiring 896 GPU-days and attaining a state-of-the-art GenEval score of 0.91. By leveraging reinforcement learning to instill Chain-of-Thought reasoning, we provide a systematic way to interpret the LLM-based searcher's internal decision-making mechanisms, revealing its optimization strategy shifted from the early-stage diversity-driven exploration to the late-stage anchor exploitation. Our proposed framework provides a scalable, generalizable, and interpretable pathway toward general-purpose open-world machine learning optimization.

papers.title: The generic behavior of permutation entropy for continuous maps
papers.summary: Permutation entropy, introduced by Bandt and Pompe in 2002, measures the complexity of a dynamical system through the ordinal patterns of its trajectories. Bandt, Keller and Pompe established that for measure-preserving, piecewise monotone interval maps with finitely many monotonicity intervals, the normalized order-$n$ permutation entropy $H_n^{\mathrm{perm}}(f)/n$ converges to the Kolmogorov--Sinai entropy. Although this result has subsequently been extended to broader classes of maps, whether normalized permutation entropy always converges has remained unknown. We show that convergence can fail, and indeed that nonconvergence is generic. More precisely, for a generic continuous Lebesgue measure-preserving map $f:[0,1]\to[0,1]$, we prove that \[ \liminf_{n\to\infty}\frac{H_n^{\mathrm{perm}}(f)}{n}=0, \qquad \limsup_{n\to\infty}\frac{H_n^{\mathrm{perm}}(f)}{n\log n}=1. \] Thus, despite the generic vanishing of Kolmogorov--Sinai entropy, permutation entropy exhibits oscillations between vanishing linear growth and the maximal possible asymptotic growth. We also construct an explicit Lebesgue measure-preserving interval map with countably many monotonicity intervals for which the normalized permutation entropy has lower limit zero and upper limit infinity. This demonstrates that nonconvergence can occur even within the countably piecewise-monotone setting, beyond the scope of the convergence theorem of Gutjahr and Keller, relying on conditions concerning the lengths of the pieces.

papers.title: Ambient-pressure superconductivity in bulk single crystals of La$_5$Ni$_4$O$_{10}$
papers.summary: Superconductivity in the Ruddlesden-Popper (RP) nickelates has so far been confined either to multilayer compounds under high pressure or to square-planar infinite-layer-type films stabilized by epitaxial strain. Here we report the high-pressure high-temperature (HPHT) growth of bulk single crystals of the quadruple-layer RP nickelate La$_5$Ni$_4$O$_{13}$ ($n=4$) and reproduce the quintuple-layer La$_6$Ni$_5$O$_{16}$ ($n=5$) synthesis, two members of the series that had previously been accessible only as thin films. Topotactic reduction of La$_5$Ni$_4$O$_{13}$ single crystals with CaH$_2$ yields the square-planar phase La$_5$Ni$_4$O$_{10}$, which we show to be a bulk, ambient-pressure superconductor with $T_\mathrm{c}^\mathrm{onset} \approx 18\,\mathrm{K}$, a shielding fraction above 60\%, and a specific-heat jump that confirms a bulk pairing transition. All crystals show besides superconductivity a coexistence with a density-wave or metal-insulator transition. The upper critical field shows a small anisotropy, $γ\approx 2.4$, which remains finite as $T \to T_c$, indicating three-dimensional superconductivity with substantial coupling between the four-layer blocks. These results identify the square-planar nickelates $R_{n+1}$Ni$_n$O$_{2n+2}$ as a bulk platform in which the layer number alone tunes the nickel valence into the superconducting regime, without chemical substitution, pressure, or epitaxial constraint.

papers.title: MarsNet: Learning the Martian Atmosphere from Observations Alone
papers.summary: We present MarsNet, a machine-learned model of the Martian atmosphere trained only on observations. Existing reanalyses assimilate spacecraft retrievals into general circulation models (GCMs), so where observations are sparse their fields largely reflect the model. We therefore use extant reanalyses only for evaluation. MarsNet alternates a two-hour forecast with an update that assimilates the observations of each window, and both steps are learned jointly. Because the Martian record is too sparse for an unrestricted network, learning is confined within a fixed physical structure: the state is in physical units, the forecast uses physical tendencies of fixed form and learned strength, and the update is a bounded Kalman update. MarsNet is trained on Mars Years (MY) 24--31 and evaluated on independent observations. On three seasons of MGS radio-occultation temperatures assimilated by no dataset, MarsNet matches or improves on the three reanalyses in the lowest three scale heights, with a near-surface root-mean-square error (RMSE) of 4.2 K against 4.4--5.4 K, but is less accurate aloft. The model's surface pressures are the most accurate of the four products (RMSE 10 Pa against Curiosity in MY32, compared with 20--46 Pa). On withheld Mars Climate Sounder profiles of MY32, its temperatures beat an observed climatology and persistence, including in ten-sol forecasts without new observations, and its stated uncertainty is close to calibrated. Much of the temperature skill is present before training and appears to come from the structure and tables fitted to the observations, while training mainly improves the surface pressures, at some cost to dust. The model cycles stably through nine Mars years, and the influence of each observation can be traced. Its speed makes experiments on the observing record practical, and it offers an independent reference for GCMs and reanalyses.

papers.title: The Minimum Canonical Volume of Threefolds of General Type
papers.summary: We prove the sharp lower bound $vol(X) \geq 1/420$ for every smooth complex projective threefold $X$ of general type.

papers.title: Brown Measures and Spectral Convergence for Arbitrary GUE Polynomials
papers.summary: For arbitrary noncommutative polynomials in independent GUE matrices, we prove that the empirical eigenvalue measure converges weakly in probability to the Brown measure of the corresponding polynomial in free semicircular variables. We also prove convergence of the entire eigenvalue set in Hausdorff distance and convergence of the spectral radius, both in probability. Equivalently, these matrix conclusions hold for arbitrary $*$-polynomials in independent complex Ginibre matrices. Independently, we prove that the support of the Brown measure of every polynomial in free semicircular variables equals its operator spectrum. The proof of weak convergence combines a criterion based on the second moment of the Brown measure with complex Gaussian rotation and convexity. The support theorem uses linearization and rigidity of matrix Dyson equations. We also prove absolute continuity for nonconstant polynomials without adjoints in free circular variables. A matrix Dyson equation recovers Brown measures of arbitrary semicircular polynomials through regularized logarithmic potentials. For drift-corrected nondegenerate elliptic free random walks, it yields quantitative convergence of potentials in the interior of the limiting domain and weak convergence of Brown measures to that of free multiplicative Brownian motion.

papers.title: Quantum Simulation of Quantum Channels and Applications
papers.summary: We review the basic theory of quantum channels and develop a strategy for simulating them on digital quantum computers, drawing upon the \emph{Choi-Kraus operator-sum representation} and Stinespring dilation to provide a unified approach for various applications. We discuss three types of applications, offering explicit examples for each: the preparation of mixed states, measurements described by positive operator-valued measures (POVMs), and the simulation of the evolution of Markovian quantum systems. We recover fundamental concepts from quantum theory, such as the purification of a mixed state and the Naimark dilation associated with a POVM. Regarding the simulation of the evolution of a Markovian quantum system, we introduce an operator, termed the residual operator, to construct, from the system's Liouvillian, a quantum channel that serves as a first-order approximation of the quantum dynamical semigroup. This allows the simulation of quantum dynamics to be performed in a manner analogous to the Euler method for ordinary differential equations, avoiding Trotterization. We prove all the theoretical results mentioned, with the exception of the fundamental Choi-Kraus theorem concerning the operator-sum representation of quantum channels, for which we provide the appropriate references. The explicit simulations discussed were implemented using the AerSimulator from IBM's Qiskit SDK, with the corresponding code available on GitHub.

papers.title: Universal semiclassical drift velocity of magnetic edge channels
papers.summary: Magnetic edge channels, arising at the edge of a two-dimensional electron gas in a magnetic field, are topologically protected and propagate unidirectionally along the edge. Their group velocities at the Fermi level, being averaged harmonically, result in drift velocity, which is related to the edge density of states, quantum capacitance, and the velocity of edge magnetoplasmons. Using semiclassical quantization of electron skipping orbits, we show that the drift velocity equals 1/2 of the electron Fermi velocity in the limit of a large number of edge channels crossing the Fermi level. This result, being universal for a hard edge and for isotropic dispersion, is checked numerically for massive electrons and for massless electrons in graphene. The drift velocity at smooth electrostatically defined edges lacks such universality. In the case of anisotropic dispersion, the semiclassical drift velocity at the hard edge reduces to a coordinate-velocity correlation along the cyclotron orbit.

papers.title: Self-Energy Construction for Chain Representations of Open Quantum Systems
papers.summary: We identify the self-energy as the environmental response to the system, which transforms covariantly under shifts of the system--environment cut. For a semi-infinite chain with asymptotically uniform parameters, this transformation admits a fixed point that defines the asymptotic boundary self-energy (BSE), whose spectral density is the Wigner semicircle. A chain-extended BSE exploits the trend of the retained chain, offering improved accuracy in representing the environment. The transformation introduces a pseudo-hyperbolic self-energy distance that is invariant under shifts of the cut, providing a natural geometry for comparing environmental responses. As a demonstration, this geometry enables cut-independent error measure of finite damped-oscillator closures of the chain, distinguishing the closure error from the chain depth error, and offers a more accurate fitting scheme than fitting the time-domain correlation function.

papers.title: Average distance and maximum induced linear forest
papers.summary: Let G be a connected graph of order n, let μ(G) denote its average distance, and let L(G) denote the maximum order of an induced linear forest of G, that is, of an induced subgraph whose components are chains. Hansen, Hertz, Kilani, Marcotte and Schindl conjectured that μ(G) {\le} L(G)/2, which can be written as 4W(G) {\le} L(G)n(n-1), where W(G) is the Wiener index of G. This inequality strengthens their bound μ(G) {\le} F(G)/2, where F(G) is the maximum order of an induced forest, as well as Chung's classical bound μ(G) {\le} α(G). In this paper we prove the conjecture for all connected graphs.
papers.comment: This paper establishes a conjecture dating back to 2009. It is 18 pages long and contains 4 figures

papers.title: The dimension of multi-index assignment polytopes and Latin-square transversal polytopes, via association schemes
papers.summary: We determine the dimensions, and the implicit equations, of several polytopes from integer programming whose vertices are the largest stable sets of highly symmetric graphs. Our main tools are two new dimension formulae within Lee's spectral method, which reads the dimension off of an association scheme: for amorphic schemes it becomes a threshold formula, and for point sets in $GF(q)^d$ invariant under the maps $z\mapsto az+b$ it is $q-1$ times the number of hyperplane directions along which some point is not equidistributed. A single integer point, a witness, then certifies a whole eigenspace. For the multi-index assignment polytopes of Appa, Magos, and Mourtos at prime-power orders, the dimension equals that of the linear relaxation except in two infinite families, which are, to our knowledge, the first counterexamples to their expectation that the two always coincide. The missing equations are explicit clique equations that the standard integer-programming formulation omits. For every abelian group with a transversal, the Latin-square transversal polytope of its Cayley table, equivalently the polytope of rainbow perfect matchings of the corresponding edge-colored $K_{n,n}$ , has the maximal dimension ${(n-1)(n-2)}$; the witnesses come from new constructions of complete mappings. We also treat transversals of Desarguesian nets and the largest sets of symmetric $3\times3$ and $4\times4$ matrices over $GF(q)$ whose differences have rank at least $3$, of sizes $q^3$ and $q^5$.

papers.title: Unified architecture for arbitrary two-qubit gates with neutral atoms
papers.summary: We propose a unified architecture for two-qubit gates in neutral-atom quantum processors which allows the implementation of the complete set of two-qubit gates. Our approach rests on a single resource that unlocks the entire gate set: an XXZ interaction with tunable anisotropy, combined only with single-qubit operations. We introduce a Rydberg-atom realization of the tunable XXZ interaction and combine it with optimally controlled global microwave pulses to implement the B, QFT, iSWAP, and $\sqrt{\mathrm{iSWAP}}$ gates, as well as a continuous gate family interpolating from CZ to iSWAP via the B gate. This work allows the implementation of any two-qubit gate natively in neutral-atom platforms, enabling flexible switching between instruction sets to reduce circuit depth and compilation overhead in quantum algorithm implementation.

papers.title: Anchor Behavior, Not Parameters: Rehearsal-Free Continual Learning with a Single Shared Prompt
papers.summary: Prompt-based continual learning adapts a frozen pre-trained vision transformer by tuning a small set of prompt tokens. Recently, one-prompt methods which share one single prompt across all tasks make this paradigm maximally parameter efficient. The open question is how a shared prompt can keep the knowledge of old classes while being updated for new ones. Existing methods protect old knowledge in parameter space, where they freeze task-specific prompts, expand new components, or sparsely gate which tokens receive gradients. However, this method sacrifices plasticity, yet the drift it still permits in shared tokens can corrupt the prompt's function on past classes. What must be preserved is the prompt's behavior. We propose TEA-Prompt, which couples (i) a token evaluation module that assigns each prompt token a continuous, input-conditional relevance score injected into the attention logits, softly specializing tokens across tasks without discarding any of them, and (ii) an attention-behavior anchoring loss that constrains each token's attention output around class-specific query regions using only compact Gaussian query statistics without stored old images, weighted by the token's past relevance. Anchoring the attention value allows the parameters to continue updating freely, as long as their interaction remains unchanged. TEA-Prompt achieves state-of-the-art accuracy with markedly lower forgetting on CIFAR-100, ImageNet-R, and CUB-200 with only 0.38M parameters. Code is publicy available at https://github.com/cuonga1cvp/TEA-Prompt.git

papers.title: Why the non-abelian Gyarmati--Matolcsi--Ruzsa inequality does not generally work: mechanisms and explicit examples
papers.summary: For finite sets in a commutative semigroup, Gyarmati, Matolcsi and Ruzsa proved \[ |A_1+\dots+A_n|^{n-1}\ \le\ \prod_{i=1}^n|A_1+\dots+A_{i-1}+A_{i+1}+\dots+A_n| . \] They asked whether in an arbitrary group \[ |A_1\cdots A_n|^{n-1}\ \le\ \prod_{i=1}^n\ \max_{a\in A_i}\,|A_1\cdots A_{i-1}\,a\,A_{i+1}\cdots A_n| , \] where each omitted set is replaced by the largest slice obtained by fixing one of its elements. Nair, Namayandeh and Zhu proved that this inequality does not hold when $n=4$ and $G=D_4^{14}$, of group order $8^{14}$. We develop its double-coset mechanism and construct counterexamples in many other groups. For $n=4$, the smallest group found has order $518\,400$, namely $A_6^2\times C_2^2$; no absolute minimality is claimed. For $n=6$ there is a witness in a group of order $1728$, for $n=10$ a class-three $3$-group of order $243$ suffices, and for $n=4$ a single class-two $2$-group of order $2^{23}$ works. We also obtain torsion-free examples. The violation ratio $R_n=|A_1\cdots A_n|^{n-1}/\prod_iN_i$ is greater than one exactly when the inequality fails; explicit four-set constructions attain $R_4\approx1.29$ in $A_8^2$, and a larger ratio of about $1.43$ is reported for $A_{10}^2$. For every $n\ge4$, the inequality holds in all direct powers of $G$ precisely when $G$ is abelian. For $n\ge2$ the optimal exponent $θ_n$ is the infimum of $\log(\prod_iN_i)/\log|A_1\cdots A_n|$ over products of size at least two. We obtain $2\leθ_n\le n-1.0768$, and an infinite family in $C_3*C_3$ shows $θ_n\le n-1-δ$ for every $δ<5-2\log_25\approx0.3561$ and all sufficiently large $n$.

papers.title: LogCDM: Interpretable Log Anomaly Detection via Behavioral Graph Drift and Adaptive Signal Fusion
papers.summary: Log-based anomaly detection is increasingly dominated by large pretrained models, from BERT-scale encoders to 8B-parameter language models, which require GPUs at inference time and are difficult to deploy on the monitoring nodes where logs are produced. We present LogCDM, a compact detector that scores each log session using three complementary signals: the next-event surprise of a small causal Transformer, the distance between a graph-attention embedding of the session's own transition graph and that of a normal reference graph, and a transition-drift statistic that we show is exactly a frequency-weighted chi-squared divergence between transition kernels. The divergence view yields an asymptotic null distribution, a length-standardized score, and a per-edge decomposition that explains each alarm. A sigmoid gate fuses the three signals; under a shared-covariance Gaussian model, this gate is the Bayes posterior, and its learned weights indicate which signal each dataset relies on. With 8.1-8.8M parameters and no GPU required at inference, LogCDM reaches F1 scores of 0.984 on HDFS, 0.870 on chronologically split BGL, and 0.850 on Thunderbird, within 0.013-0.12 of an 8.1B-parameter LLM detector evaluated under the same protocol and above all compact baselines on BGL. It scores a session in 5.5-10.5 ms on a CPU. Ablations show that the structural signals add 0.025-0.030 F1 on BGL and Thunderbird but almost nothing on HDFS, consistent with the learned fusion weights.

papers.title: Search for Dark Photon Dark Matter at 74--159 $μ$eV/$c^2$ Using Broadband Cryogenic Receivers
papers.summary: Dark photons are hypothetical massive vector bosons that couple to ordinary photons through kinetic mixing $χ$. Dark photon dark matter (DPDM) converts into photons at a metal surface, with a frequency set by its mass. Using cryogenic K- and Ka-band receivers with a broadband spectrometer, we searched for this signal over 74--159 $μ$eV/$c^2$ (18--38.5 GHz) with an integration time of $4.8\times10^5$ s per frequency bin. We found no statistically significant signal and set upper limits of $χ<(3.1$--$17)\times10^{-12}$ at the 95% confidence level over 99.8% of the search range, assuming DPDM constitutes all local dark matter. These results improve on previous limits by more than an order of magnitude over most of 74--110 $μ$eV/$c^2$ and provide the first direct limits over most of 110--159 $μ$eV/$c^2$, approximately two orders of magnitude below cosmological bounds.

papers.title: An efficient classical algorithm for OTOCs in chaotic quantum dynamics
papers.summary: Estimating out-of-time-ordered correlators (OTOCs) in individual instances of random quantum circuits has been proposed as a candidate for verifiable quantum advantage, and demonstrated to be hard for conventional classical algorithms such as tensor networks and Monte Carlo. Using insights from quantum chaos, we develop and implement a polynomial-time classical algorithm for the four-point ${\rm OTOC}^{(1)}$ and the eight-point ${\rm OTOC}^{(2)}$ in typical instances of one-dimensional (1D) quantum circuits. Our results demonstrate average-case classical tractability of estimating OTOCs in the sensitive regime where circuit-to-circuit fluctuations are large. Our algorithm organizes the OTOC into a rapidly converging series, where the leading term includes contributions from histories within permutation degrees of freedom in the replicated Hilbert space, and subleading terms arise from excursions outside this space. Although chaos is often viewed as an insurmountable barrier to classical simulation, our algorithm exploits a form of dephasing caused by chaos, which suppresses the subleading terms. We provide strong theoretical and numerical evidence to support this suppression. Further, we demonstrate that practical implementations of our algorithm estimate ${\rm OTOC}^{(1)}$ and ${\rm OTOC}^{(2)}$ in 1D circuits with high accuracy, achieving higher signal-to-noise ratio at larger circuit depths compared to recent 2D experiments by Google. Extending our algorithm to higher dimensions, and resolving the status of quantum advantage in 2D OTOCs, remain open problems.

papers.title: Gravitational waves and the exit from de Sitter in Inflation without an Inflaton
papers.summary: In Inflation without an Inflaton (IWI), second-order de Sitter (dS) gravitons generate primordial curvature as the Coulomb-type potential of their gradient stress. Each pair contributes $(p/k)^2$, yielding exponential enhancement over the contributing e-folds. With exact Bunch-Davies evolution, this solution satisfies all four scalar second-order Einstein equations in pure dS. The retarded transverse-traceless solution instead has a UV kernel of order unity, $(k/p)^2$ below the scalar kernel, and a one-loop correction $Δ^2_{h,2}/Δ^2_h\simeq0.04\,Δ^2_h$. Its source acts before internal freeze-out, but oscillatory cancellations prevent tensor enhancement. We evolve the curvature through a smooth exit into radiation domination. Conserved curvature resides on the vacuum-decay hypersurface. A global depletion clock holds each scale on zero-shear time for $N_{\rm w}$ e-folds after horizon exit before local release, giving all scales equal enhancement. Energy-momentum conservation feeds the depleted vacuum energy into a non-vacuum sector, modeled as radiation. Deep in radiation domination, $Δ^2_ζ=c_wΔ_h^4e^{N_{\rm w}}/20$, with clock-dependent $c_w$, $n_s-1=-4ε$, and $n_T=-2ε$. The spectrum is adiabatic and Gaussian; super-horizon $ζ$ is conserved to better than $10^{-4}$, and changing the adiabatic exit fluid alters it by less than $0.2\%$. A direct radiation exit requires $31\lesssim N_{\rm w}\lesssim50$, or $3\times10^{-6}\lesssim r\lesssim0.036$. At interferometer frequencies, $Ω_{\rm GW}h^2\simeq2\times10^{-21}$--$3\times10^{-17}$, accessible to BBO for $r\gtrsim0.01$ and ultimate DECIGO for $r\gtrsim10^{-5}$; CMB B-mode searches probe $r\gtrsim10^{-3}$. Above $k_{\rm end}e^{-N_{\rm w}}$, the scalar spectrum steepens to $k^{-1}$, suppressing $μ$-distortions for sharp release when $N_{\rm w}\gtrsim45$.

papers.title: The structure of the pion at large $N_c$
papers.summary: We compute the pion quark momentum fraction in the large-$N_c$ limit using the Twisted Eguchi-Kawai (TEK) reduced model. Gauge configurations for different values of the lattice spacing are generated with the pure-gauge TEK action, while the pion correlators are computed for different quark masses with maximally twisted mass fermions. The bare matrix element corresponding to the quark momentum fraction is obtained using the Feynman-Hellmann method, and we use perturbative renormalization factors to connect to the $\overline{\mathrm{MS}}$ scheme at $2\,\mathrm{GeV}$. A global analysis at several lattice spacings, pion masses, and values of $N_c$ yields $\langle x\rangle_q^{\overline{\mathrm{MS}}}(2\,\mathrm{GeV}) = 0.267(105)$ at the physical pion mass in the large-$N_c$ limit. This value is significantly smaller than existing $N_c=3$ determinations from phenomenology and lattice QCD, indicating that, in the large-$N_c$ limit, the pion's light-cone momentum is carried predominantly by gluons.

papers.title: Learning Rate Decay Can Exponentially Accelerate SGD for Global Optimization of Nonconvex Functions
papers.summary: Stochastic Gradient Descent (SGD) is a workhorse algorithm for continuous optimization. It is a folk belief among deep learning practitioners that learning rate decay in SGD substantially improves performance. However, it has remained unclear whether learning rate decay offers an asymptotic advantage for global nonconvex optimization. We answer this question in the affirmative by demonstrating a natural class of nonconvex functions for which, we prove that SGD with learning rate decay requires exponentially fewer gradient queries for global optimization than SGD with any fixed learning rate in the small-step size regime. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first exponential advantage that has been demonstrated for learning rate decay. The class of functions we consider includes many popular benchmark nonconvex functions. Our results provide a robust explanatory theory for the empirically observed benefits of learning rate decay for global optimization. We show that annealing performs the non-logconcave sampling task associated to the optimization problem in polynomial time, via a novel application of weak Poincaré inequalities.

papers.title: Adaptive Output Regulation of Linear Systems with Unknown Harmonic Exosystems and Additive Noise
papers.summary: This paper addresses error-feedback output regulation for known multivariable linear plants subject to an unknown exosystem and additive Gaussian process and measurement noise. The exosystem generates constant and sinusoidal signals, but its dimension, frequencies, and coupling matrices are unavailable. An output-injection transformation represents the external action through known channels. A causal observer then produces a residual independent of the applied input, whose filtered output separates into a harmonic signal, stationary colored Gaussian noise, and a decaying transient. Using this observation model, a Fourier procedure consistently identifies the number and values of the active positive frequencies in the presence of noise. The identified frequencies determine a regulator through interpolation with stable residual filters. A contractive filter realization, nonexpansive state resizing, and bounded gain updates ensure closed-loop moment bounds uniformly over the selected filter orders. If the gain bound contains the ideal interpolation gain, the adaptive plant response and tracking error converge in mean square to those of the corresponding known-frequency regulator. The limiting mean-square tracking error is a linear function of the process- and measurement-noise covariances. In the absence of both noises, the tracking error converges to zero.

papers.title: Certified Zonotopic Reachability Analysis for Trajectory Tracking on Lie Groups
papers.summary: Autonomous vehicles track planned trajectories close to obstacles. Unknown disturbances make them deviate from these trajectories. With a bound on the tracking error that disturbances can cause, a planned trajectory can be certified as safe before execution. Existing set-based methods bound the tracking error by one invariant ellipsoid for the whole trajectory or by intervals, which are both conservative. For aerial and space vehicles, the tracking error evolves on a matrix Lie group with nonlinear dynamics. However, for group-affine systems, the error dynamics are linear in Lie algebra coordinates when the vehicle receives the inputs of the reference. The control input and the disturbance enter through the inverse right Jacobian, a matrix that depends on the error. We propagate the linear part of the error dynamics with zonotopes and enclose the effect of the inverse right Jacobian on the disturbance in closed form. The resulting tubes are tight and provably contain all reachable tracking errors in continuous time. When some error components have no input, the inverse right Jacobian leaves unmatched nonlinear terms in the closed loop. None of the tested methods certifies such a closed loop. Hybrid coordinates make these terms matched, so that our controller cancels every nonlinear term that does not contain the disturbance. Our tubes give tighter bounds than the ellipsoid method in simulations of a planar aircraft and a fully actuated multirotor and in real flights of a quadrotor, where the tube contains every measured attitude error. Under larger disturbances and the same feedback gain, the ellipsoid method yields no valid ellipsoid, whereas our tubes remain valid.

papers.title: Riemannian Real-Time Optimization for Robotics: Active Set SQP Parametric Pathfollowing
papers.summary: Robot optimal control often combines Euclidean states with configurations on Lie groups and other smooth manifolds. This paper develops a parametric Riemannian Newton pathfollowing method based on homotopy quadratic programs and parallel strict-working-set tasks. It specifies the event handling, working-set exchanges, matrix factor updates, synchronization, and residual checks used by the algorithm. Tracking guarantees are given under mildly degenerate regularity conditions and the Riemannian strong second-order sufficient condition. Drone navigation and arm manipulation are formulated as geometric optimal-control problems, including finite-force grasp acquisition, transport and supported release. Numerical examples illustrate drone navigation and arm pick-and-place through KKT-residual histories and MuJoCo simulations, together with preliminary initialization results for the full-horizon optimal-control problems.

papers.title: Quality time in extra dimensions: axion quality and radion cosmology
papers.summary: Higher-form symmetries can protect extra-dimensional axions, but additional symmetry breaking can still spoil the solution to the strong CP problem. We focus on electrically charged matter and magnetic gauging in a five-dimensional circle compactification where the axion arises from an Abelian gauge field and the radius is dynamical. We discuss two mechanisms for stabilising the radius/radion using Casimir energy from fields neutral under the Abelian gauge field, with and without an additional periodic scalar winding around the compact circle. Both admit Minkowski and de Sitter minima. At the Minkowski minima (with radion masses of $100$--$170\,\mathrm{TeV}$), electrically charged matter induces a residual strong CP angle of order $10^{-17}$ and shifts the radius negligibly. Magnetic gauging remains compatible after including its additional degree of freedom in the Casimir spectrum, provided its coupling is sufficiently small. We observe that increasing the radius suppresses charged-matter breaking relative to QCD but increases magnetic breaking contribution. We also determine the radion decay channels, including the graviphoton, and study reheating from a possible radion-dominated era without scalar winding or magnetic gauging. For a non-minimal Higgs-curvature coupling $ξ=7$, the visible-sector reheating temperature is about $85\,\mathrm{MeV}$ with a dark-radiation contribution of $ΔN_{\rm eff}\approx0.02$. The entropy released during radion decay dilutes the axion abundance, allowing axions with $f_a=10^{14}\,\mathrm{GeV}$ and an initial misalignment angle $\vartheta_i\approx0.43$ to account for the entire observed dark matter abundance. For the same decay constant, reproducing this abundance in radiation domination requires $\vartheta_i\approx0.065$.

papers.title: PORT: Preference Optimization via Robust Token-Level Reweighting
papers.summary: Preference optimization has become a central approach for aligning large language models with human values, but its effectiveness depends heavily on the quality of preference annotations. In practice, preference data is often noisy due to annotation errors and ambiguity. Existing robust preference optimization methods primarily operate at the sequence level, implicitly treating entire responses as uniformly correct or incorrect. However, rejected responses may still contain informative reasoning steps, while preferred responses can include subtle errors. In this work, we propose \textbf{P}reference \textbf{O}ptimization via \textbf{R}obust \textbf{T}oken-level reweighting \textbf{(PORT)}, a fine-grained framework for robust alignment under noisy preferences. PORT performs token-level reweighting using the empirical cumulative distribution function (CDF) of token log-probabilities, yielding an efficient forward-pass-only proxy to gradient-norm penalization that selectively suppresses corrupted tokens without additional backward-pass computation. We provide theoretical analysis showing that PORT reduces the gradient bias from noisy preference labels by minimizing an upper bound on the bias term. Extensive experiments across diverse noise settings demonstrate that PORT consistently improves robustness and outperforms existing sequence-level baselines. The code is available at https://github.com/osu-srml/PORT

papers.title: Sage-Taiyi: A Metacognitive Architecture for Scientific Discovery
papers.summary: We introduce Sage-Taiyi, a metacognition-inspired architecture that uses accumulated scientific understanding to guide what to investigate next and how to investigate it. Through explicit monitoring and control, the system revises its understanding of evidence, assumptions, and unresolved questions, then uses these assessments to adapt research targets and select reusable reasoning methods. On Taiyi-Bench, an AI co-scientist ideation benchmark comprising 265 tasks from 50 papers across ten disciplines, Sage-Taiyi ranks first on all eight metrics of historical rediscovery and open-ended ideation, achieving an Overall score of 54.0 compared with 47.9 for the strongest baseline, AI Scientist-v2. It also performs well on two external scientific ideation benchmarks. Five expert-guided collaborations further connect its proposals to experimental and computational validation across chemistry, materials science, and engineering. In chemistry, reaction-condition optimization raises the yield of cobalt-catalyzed carbonylation from trace amounts to 84% and photocatalytic allylic amination from 13% to 69%. These results support metacognitive regulation as an approach to scientific ideation and its progression toward practical validation.

papers.title: A Hoare Logic for Continuous-Time Stochastic Processes
papers.summary: Programming language researchers have developed a wide array of tools to reason about probabilistic programs, but it remains unclear how to apply these proof techniques to continuous-time stochastic processes. To bridge this gap, we propose a verification method for properties of continuous-time stochastic processes by reasoning about them as standard programs.
